Taking each clause on evidence: "basically free" holds ($0.042/M input, output free, models.md 2026-09-24). "Insanely good" has n=0 in this repo — grep finds no Jev integration, no eval, no log — so it is an unmeasured anecdote from projects that are not Joycraft, and my lens must refuse it as a basis for a core feature. "Route what files to look at, what pointers in the context map, help claude code with tool calls" — none of these three has a single measurement in the pack, in TypeSafe's cookbooks, or on TypeSafe's coding-agents page, which explicitly does not position Jev on a coding agent's prompt path. The only routing evidence (skills) was produced on jev-1.12 with Haiku 4.5 over 182 skills on a proprietary, vendor-authored test set the vendor itself calls easier than real user requests — and the maintainer's own thesis (§0) is that frontier models, not Haiku, are the target. The maintainer also wrote "I'm open to the skeptics saying no of course." My lens says no to "core" and "hot path": the citations that hold (MCA updated yesterday, AS IS, no SLA, three incidents in five days, a hook that stalls the session until timeout, a model that treats injected state as data) all point away from the hot path, and the one citation that would have to carry the proposition does not transfer. This moves the position from "core, hot path, for anyone with a key" to an opt-in experiment, off the hot path, that ships only after (1) the model-free forced-eval baseline is measured on Joycraft's 22-skill roster with Fable/Opus as the agent, and (2) a jev-1.13 run over that same roster and a request set not written from the skills' own SKILL.md shows a delta above the forced-eval baseline. Until both numbers exist, the claim that Jev is "too good" not to be core is a claim without a source.


### P7 — Hybrid distribution: two skill dirs, a Claude plugin, the CLI, no MCP main channel

**Ruling: QUALIFY.** Three of P7's four legs stand on verified evidence: one skills tree published to .agents/skills and .claude/skills, the CLI as carrier of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, hooks, settings patches, templates, check.mjs and Pi runtime files, and no MCP server as the main channel. The fourth leg, "a Claude Code plugin for the Claude runtime (namespacing, eval delta, install hints)", holds only when the plugin is a project-scope skills-directory plugin that the CLI writes and git commits (a .claude-plugin/plugin.json inside the project's .claude/skills/), not a marketplace-distributed plugin, and only with "install hints" struck from its benefit list. A marketplace plugin is refuted for now on the repo's own 2026-03 deferral rule and on Claude Code's documented update semantics.

**Claim as argued:** Publish one skills tree to .agents/skills and .claude/skills, ship a Claude Code plugin for the Claude runtime (namespacing, eval delta, install hints), keep the CLI for cross-harness files and per-host hooks, and do not build an MCP server as the main channel. Skeptic angles: the 2026-03 deferral reason was avoiding two distribution formats; third-party plugin auto-update is off by default; a plugin cannot carry CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md; Compound Engineering warns plugin updates strand users; the git-based skills installer moves 28M installs a month and might replace the CLI entirely.

**Replacement claim:** Distribution: one harness-neutral skills tree published to .agents/skills and .claude/skills; the CLI as the single install and update channel carrying CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, hooks, settings patches, templates, check.mjs and Pi runtime files; a Claude Code plugin only in the form of a git-committed project-scope skills-directory manifest the CLI writes into .claude/skills/ (namespacing and `claude plugin eval` delta, no install hints, no marketplace, no second version string); a marketplace plugin deferred until the skill set is stable and either official-marketplace listing or a manifest plugin-version kind exists; no MCP server as the main channel.

**Condition:** P7 holds when, and only when: (1) 'Claude plugin' means a project-scope skills-directory plugin, a .claude-plugin/plugin.json the CLI writes and git commits inside the project's .claude/skills/, loaded as joycraft@skills-dir with no marketplace, no separate version string, and no second release step, used for `claude plugin eval` in CI and, if and when skills are renamed, for /joycraft:<name> namespacing; a marketplace plugin is deferred until the P1/P4/P8 skill reshaping has shipped and skill content has been stable for at least one quarter, and then only if Joycraft is listed in claude-plugins-official or the install manifest gains an ownership kind recording plugin version beside CLI version; (2) 'install hints' is struck from the plugin's benefit list; (3) 'one skills tree to .agents/skills and .claude/skills' ships with harness-neutral bodies (no {{skill_prefix}}, {{clear}}, {{skills_dir}} substitutions in prose, invocation and session-reset moved to a per-harness header or AGENTS.md router line) or with a verified shadowing per-harness copy, after checking that hosts reading both dirs (Copilot, Cursor, Amp, OpenCode, omp) dedupe by name and after reconciling Joycraft's .pi/skills install target with Pi's actual runtime read path; (4) the CLI remains the sole carrier of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, hooks, settings patches, templates, check.mjs and Pi runtime files, and the update channel for every harness; (5) any eval delta measured with `claude plugin eval` gates Claude-specific content only, never the shared tree, unless the shared tree is also evaluated on at least one open-weight model; (6) no MCP server as the main channel, which needs no condition.

**Judge's reasoning:** All four skeptics returned "qualified" and converged on the same fault line, which is unusual enough to be evidence in itself: nobody attacked the two-dir tree, the CLI's role, or "no MCP main channel" on the merits; every attack landed on the marketplace plugin. I verified the pivot they all rely on. code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md (fetched 2026-09-24) states verbatim that a plugin directory with a .claude-plugin/plugin.json saved under the project's .claude/skills/ loads as `<name>@skills-dir`, that "A project-scope plugin is checked into the repository and reaches every collaborator who clones it", that it loads in place and is never copied, and that no marketplace is involved. The same page confirms the three facts that sink the marketplace form: auto-update is "off for every other marketplace" besides Anthropic's official ones and claude.ai-added ones; "The running session keeps the versions it loaded" after a random delay of up to ten minutes; and "a manifest that pins "version": "1.0.0" keeps every user on the cached copy until its author changes the string, however many commits they push". It also confirms the team-lead's sharpest point: "When a plugin's only true is in the project's .claude/settings.json, Claude Code doesn't fetch it onto a machine where it isn't installed", so a committed enabledPlugins entry does not propagate a marketplace plugin to the 15 colleagues. The two benefits the pack credits to the plugin that actually exist, namespacing and `claude plugin eval` delta, are available from the skills-dir form (all four skeptics cite cli-reference.md's `name@skills-dir` target; I did not spend my one fetch on it because none of them disputed it). The third benefit, install hints, is unavailable: cli-hints.md restricts it to claude-plugins-official or another Anthropic-named marketplace, which the pack's own section 2.7 already said and the section 2 inference then ignored. The 2026-03 deferral holds in the repo verbatim (docs/features/plugin-architecture/research.md:55, "Package as plugin once feature set is stable to avoid iterating on two distribution formats") and its condition is further away, not closer, since P1/P4/P8 propose reshaping all 22 skills. Coupling makes the skew concrete: the canonical skills reference docs/templates/ 77 times and docs/.joycraft/ 13 times (my grep), all CLI-installed, and src/install-manifest.ts:30 has no ownership kind that records a plugin version beside the CLI version. On the two-dir leg, the maintainer and repo-explorer evidence (§8.8: dropped skills removed cleanly) show the five-to-two collapse needs no new machinery, and §3.3 shows two dirs reach every surveyed harness because Claude Code alone ignores .agents/skills. That leg stands, but with a caveat the pack understates: today's per-harness trees differ by skill_prefix, clear, and skills_dir substitutions (scripts/lib/skill-template.mjs:11-46, 141 prefix sites) plus real body forks in research, implement-feature, verify and lockdown, so "one tree" to .agents/skills means harness-neutral prose or a shadowing per-harness copy, not a byte copy of today's Claude variant. "No MCP main channel" drew no serious attack from any lens and rests on verified facts (Pi ships no MCP, Agent Plugins 1.0 excludes hooks, skills-over-MCP has near-zero adoption); it stands without condition. The "git-based installer might replace the CLI" angle fails on all four returns: vercel-labs/skills installs SKILL.md files only, no hooks, AGENTS.md, settings, templates or Pi runtime; it can replace the plugin's job, not the CLI's.

**Strongest refutation considered:** The maintainer's return is the strongest because it converts every plugin benefit into something the CLI already produces or can produce with one file, and then prices the residual as pure cost: a skills-dir manifest gives `/joycraft:` namespacing and a `claude plugin eval` target with no marketplace; install hints are unavailable to a non-official marketplace regardless; what a marketplace adds is a second version string, a second release step on a ~weekly cadence (16 v0.7.x tags in nine weeks), auto-update off by default, and a version skew between plugin-served skill text and CLI-served templates that the manifest cannot detect. Combined with the team-lead's observation that a committed enabledPlugins entry does not fetch a marketplace plugin onto a teammate's machine, this refutes the marketplace form outright rather than merely qualifying it. I considered whether to flip the whole proposition on this basis and did not, because the maintainer's own argument leaves the other three legs intact and supplies the exact replacement shape for the fourth; a flip would discard verified content to punish one word.

**Key evidence:**
- A plugin directory with .claude-plugin/plugin.json under the project's .claude/skills/ loads as <name>@skills-dir, in place, with no marketplace; 'A project-scope plugin is checked into the repository and reaches every collaborator who clones it.' — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md, 'Find where a plugin came from' table and 'Plugins shared through a repository' (verified by judge, 2026-09-24)
- Auto-update default is 'on for Anthropic's official marketplaces such as claude-plugins-official ... on for marketplaces added from claude.ai, and off for every other marketplace'; running session keeps loaded versions after a random delay of up to ten minutes. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md, 'When auto-update runs' and 'Which marketplaces and plugins auto-update' (verified by judge)
- 'a manifest that pins "version": "1.0.0" keeps every user on the cached copy until its author changes the string, however many commits they push.' — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md, 'How Claude Code computes the version' (verified by judge)
- 'When a plugin's only true is in the project's .claude/settings.json, Claude Code doesn't fetch it onto a machine where it isn't installed' unless the marketplace entry has a relative-path source or a seed directory holds it. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md, 'Enabled in project settings but not installed' (verified by judge)
- The 2026-03 deferral already recommended the CLI+plugin hybrid and deferred it: 'Package as plugin once feature set is stable to avoid iterating on two distribution formats.' — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/docs/features/plugin-architecture/research.md:1-4,51-55 (verified by judge)
- Skills are coupled to CLI-installed files: 77 references to docs/templates/ and 13 to docs/.joycraft/ across src/skills/*.md; 141 {{skill_prefix}} sites; per-harness LOOKUP differs in skill_prefix, clear, skills_dir. — grep over /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/skills/*.md and /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/scripts/lib/skill-template.mjs:11-46 (verified by judge)
- The manifest has no ownership kind that could record a plugin version beside the CLI version. — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/install-manifest.ts:30, ManifestFileKind = 'vendor' | 'create-once' | 'config-patch' (verified by judge)
- Install hints apply only to plugins in claude-plugins-official or another Anthropic-named marketplace; claude-community is excluded; no prompt in -p, subagent, cloud, or analytics-off sessions. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-hints.md (four skeptics, fetched 2026-09-24; consistent with pack §2.7)
- `claude plugin eval` accepts a plugin directory or name@skills-dir as target, so the eval delta needs no distribution channel. — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference.md, 'plugin eval' (maintainer, team-lead, evidence-auditor; undisputed)
- The `skills` npm CLI (28,522,027 downloads 2026-08-23 to 2026-09-21) installs SKILL.md files only: no hooks beyond Claude Code and Kiro, no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, settings, templates or Pi runtime. — https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-month/skills and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/skills/main/README.md (all four skeptics; consistent with pack §3.7)
- Release cadence is ~weekly: 16 v0.7.x tags between 2026-07-22 and 2026-09-23. — git tag --sort=creatordate in /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft (verified by judge)
- Dropping trees needs no new manifest machinery: dropped skills are removed cleanly, edited copies kept as orphans. — Evidence pack §8.8; /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/install-manifest.ts adoption loop (maintainer, solo-pi)

**Skeptic disagreements:**
- Compound Engineering 'strands users' citation: maintainer and solo-pi mark it 'holds' (quote verbatim in README); team-lead and evidence-auditor mark it 'misread' because the README's '/plugin update alone keeps you on the old version' refers to a one-time layout migration needing a marketplace refresh first, not a general hazard. Judge: the quote is real, the generalization in the P7 skeptic angle is overstated; the mechanism that does generalize is loading.md's version-pin and auto-update-off rules, which I verified directly.
- Whether the skills-dir plugin should replace or sit beside the flat joycraft-* tree: team-lead's qualification requires it to replace the flat tree (otherwise 44 descriptions double-list); maintainer says renaming breaks 141 {{skill_prefix}} references, the legacy detector at src/install-manifest.ts:351,372, and the 2026-03-24 decision 'Never — namespacing is the right pattern', and that unrenamed skills namespace as /joycraft:joycraft-tune. Unresolved: the replacement form has a real rename cost no skeptic priced.
- Which directory Pi actually reads: evidence-auditor says Joycraft installs to .pi/skills, which current Pi docs do not list (docs list .agents/skills only); solo-pi says Pi's coding-agent resource-loader.ts hard-codes <cwd>/.pi/skills and the .agents/skills read is found only in a test in packages/agent, not traced to runtime. Both unverified; they point opposite ways on whether the two-dir tree reaches Pi at all.
- Copilot dedupe across .claude/skills and .agents/skills: team-lead quotes docs.github.com 'Skills are deduplicated by their name field' with precedence .github > .agents > .claude; evidence-auditor says the same page states no precedence or dedupe rule. Direct contradiction on one page; not resolved here.
- Claude-gated block counts: maintainer reports 38 claude-gated blocks, team-lead 44 '<!-- harness:claude -->' blocks, evidence-auditor per-file counts (implement-feature 10, research 4, verify 4, lockdown 3); my grep finds 75 '<!-- harness:' markers total across src/skills. The counts differ by whether closing markers and multi-harness gates are included; the substance (forks concentrate in three or four skills) is not disputed.
- What the two-dir collapse saves: maintainer says almost no hours, because cost lives in the content forks not the tree count; solo-pi and evidence-auditor say one tree is a correctness problem (Pi reads Codex prose) unless bodies go harness-neutral; team-lead says it means shipping Claude-only prose to Codex or deleting it. Compatible but distinct: hours vs correctness vs content loss.
- Eval delta gating: solo-pi alone conditions the plugin on its claude plugin eval delta never gating the shared tree, since eval runs only on a Claude model and the inverted-U literature says frontier-tuned pruning removes what open-weight users need. No other skeptic addresses this; the maintainer treats the eval delta as a plain benefit.
- Team asymmetry: team-lead alone raises that a Claude plugin with no Codex counterpart is an asymmetry a mixed team notices, citing Codex's own plugin surface (unverified). No other lens engages it.
- Whether the 2026-03 deferral wording lives in the research doc or the draft brief: solo-pi and evidence-auditor locate it in docs/features/plugin-architecture/research.md:55 (also at commit 9aa8edd as docs/research/plugin-architecture.md); the 2026-03-26 draft brief's 'Why Not Now' gives different reasons (evolving plugin system, breaking name change, unknown distribution). All agree the deferral is real; they disagree on where the date attaches.

**Citation problems:**
- P7 skeptic angle 'Compound Engineering warns plugin updates strand users' overstates the source: the README line '/plugin update alone keeps you on the old version' describes a one-time layout migration that needed a marketplace refresh first (team-lead, evidence-auditor). The general stranding mechanism exists but lives in loading.md's version-pin and auto-update rules, not in the CE README.
- P7 skeptic angle 'the git-based skills installer ... might replace the CLI entirely' is refuted by the installer's own README: it installs skill files only. All four skeptics checked it.
- Evidence pack §2 inference lists 'CLI hints' as a plugin benefit while §2.7 on the same page says hints are official-marketplace only; the inference contradicts its own fact and should drop hints.
- Evidence pack §2.2 '1% of context listing budget': evidence-auditor could not find the figure on skills.md (found 1,536-char truncation and 25,000-token re-attach budget instead). Not dead, but unlocated.
- Evidence pack §5 'CE removed a schema field so Codex stops truncating skills at 8KB': not in the CE README or CHANGELOG; evidence-auditor located it in docs/specs/agent-plugins.md (MAX_SKILL_PROMPT_BYTES 8000, Codex >=0.147). The claim holds but the pack cites the wrong location.
- agentplugins.dev failed TLS handshake for the evidence-auditor (dead for that fetch); the Agent Plugins 1.0 facts were confirmed instead via vercel.com/blog and github.blog.
- Evidence pack §2.6 'Cloud sessions don't load local plugins': only partially verified (loading.md says cloud sessions never show the trust dialog and so skip repo extraKnownMarketplaces and project skills-dir plugins; --plugin-dir in cloud not directly tested).
- Team-lead's claim about Codex plugins (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins bundling skills, MCP, hooks; no repo-level pinning) is self-marked UNVERIFIED.
- Evidence pack §3 table row 'Pi: .agents/skills' vs Joycraft's install target .pi/skills (skill-template.mjs:28): the pack does not note that Joycraft's Pi install location is absent from current Pi docs, and the Pi runtime's actual read path is untraced (solo-pi vs evidence-auditor).
- The date on the deferral: the pack attributes it to '2026-03'; the verbatim wording is in docs/features/plugin-architecture/research.md (dated 2026-03-24), while docs/features/2026-03-26-plugin-migration-draft/brief.md gives different 'Why Not Now' reasons. Holds, but the two documents are not interchangeable.

**What would change the ruling:** Toward keep-as-written (marketplace plugin viable): Anthropic accepting Joycraft into claude-plugins-official, which turns auto-update on by default and makes install hints available; or Claude Code adding a marketplace.json field that turns on auto-update for third-party marketplaces; or a manifest ownership kind that records the plugin version beside the CLI version so skew becomes detectable by tune/optimize. Toward flip (drop the plugin leg entirely, even the skills-dir form): evidence that a project-scope skills-dir plugin fails to load in the `claude -p` or subagent sessions Joycraft's queue loops and headless vision depend on (loading.md says 'running with -p isn't enough' for the trust check; whether an already-trusted folder suffices is untested), or that a skills-dir plugin cannot coexist with plain .claude/skills siblings without double-listing, or that the rename to /joycraft:<name> costs more than the namespacing is worth. Toward weakening the two-dir leg: Claude Code adding .agents/skills as a project skill location (drops the .claude/skills copy), verification that Cursor, Amp, OpenCode or Copilot list a same-named skill twice across the two dirs, or a trace showing Pi's runtime does not read project-level .agents/skills. Nothing plausible would change the 'no MCP main channel' clause short of a mainstream client shipping skills-over-MCP and Pi adopting MCP.

**Human position moved?** Section 10 holds no direct P7 answer; two answers bear on it and the panel moved both, unanimously across four lenses. Q3, "all I have to do is push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice": every skeptic showed that a third-party marketplace plugin is the opposite of a push channel (auto-update off by default per loading.md, cache refresh on a random delay of up to ten minutes, running session keeps the old copy until /reload-plugins, version string pinned by the maintainer's manifest, committed enabledPlugins not fetched onto teammates' machines). The channel that already does 'push and everyone gets it' is the one Joycraft has: the CLI's per-skill-entry check.mjs plus src/auto-safe-update.ts, and git for committed files. The wish stands; the plugin is the wrong instrument for it. Q2, "about 15 colleagues all of use it daily driver, across different size teams": the 2026-03 research table the maintainer himself accepted scored this ('Team sharing: Git commit' vs 'Each dev installs plugin'), and the team-lead showed that a plugin puts skill text on each laptop's update schedule while the templates, hooks and check.mjs those skills cite 90 times stay on the repo's, which is exactly the population size where skew surfaces. One further move: the maintainer's own 2026-03 recommendation was 'Both: plugin + CLI', deferred until stable; the panel does not overturn that recommendation, it sharpens it to a git-committed skills-dir plugin that costs no second release train and keeps one distribution format, and it re-affirms the deferral of the marketplace form because P0-P11 make the skill set less stable, not more. Q4 ('gates that cannot be overridden') is touched only by the team-lead: a gate one engineer hits on one skill version and another does not is a gate teams route around; the qualified form avoids that split.

#### Skeptics

##### Maintainer counting hours — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** Three of P7's four parts cost me nothing or save me hours; the fourth, a Claude plugin as a distribution channel, buys nothing I cannot already get and adds a second release train. Evidence, all live-checked 2026-09-24: (1) Namespacing does not need a marketplace. A `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` saved under the project's `.claude/skills/` loads as a `joycraft@skills-dir` plugin with `/joycraft:<skill>` prefixes (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md, "Find where a plugin came from"). The CLI already writes that directory. And the prefix stays even when frontmatter sets `name` (components.md line 662 of fetched copy), so shipping today's `joycraft-tune` as a plugin yields `/joycraft:joycraft-tune` unless I rename 22 skills, which breaks 141 `{{skill_prefix}}` cross-references (src/skills/*.md), the `joycraft-*` legacy detector (src/install-manifest.ts:351,372), and the 2026-03-24 decision "Never — namespacing is the right pattern" (docs/context/decision-log.md:101). (2) Eval delta does not need a marketplace. `claude plugin eval [target]` takes "A plugin directory" or `name@skills-dir` and runs the with/without ablation from CI (plugins/cli-reference.md, "plugin eval"). A local manifest plus a CI step gets the Δ. (3) Install hints are unavailable to Joycraft. The hint page "applies only if your plugin is listed in claude-plugins-official or another marketplace with one of Anthropic's official marketplace names. The community marketplace, claude-community, isn't one of them" (plugins/cli-hints.md). Also blocked in `-p` runs, subagents, cloud, and when telemetry is off. (4) What the marketplace channel adds is cost: auto-update is "off for your marketplace by default, and marketplace.json has no field to turn it on" (plugins/host-marketplace.md, "Turn on auto-update"; loading.md "The default: ... off for every other marketplace"); a bumped `version` is the only update signal, so each of my ~weekly releases gains a plugin.json/marketplace.json bump plus a publish step in scripts/automatic-release.mjs and the docs-sync gate; and Compound Engineering's README confirms the failure mode: "Running /plugin update alone keeps you on the old version." Worse for Joycraft specifically: skills reference `docs/templates/` 77 times and `docs/.joycraft/` 13 times (grep over src/skills/*.md). A plugin skill at version N+1 talking to CLI-installed templates, hooks, and check.mjs at version N is a skew the manifest (src/install-manifest.ts:30, kinds vendor | create-once | config-patch) has no kind for. A Claude user with both the plugin and the CLI-installed `.claude/skills` also lists 44 descriptions against the 1% budget the pack itself says to protect (evidence pack §2.2), unless I write new detection logic to suppress one, which is a new mechanism. (5) The 2026-03 deferral condition is further away, not closer: "Package as plugin once feature set is stable to avoid iterating on two distribution formats" (docs/features/plugin-architecture/research.md:55). P0-P11 propose rewriting every skill. Packaging a plugin now means iterating two formats through the churn the deferral was written to avoid.

**Qualification:** P7 stands for the two skill directories (`.agents/skills` + `.claude/skills`), for keeping the CLI as the carrier of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, hooks, settings patches, templates, check.mjs, and Pi runtime files, and for no MCP main channel. It is refuted for a Claude plugin distributed through a marketplace. Exact condition under which the plugin part survives: ship the plugin only as a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest that the CLI writes inside the project's `.claude/skills/` (a skills-directory plugin), with no marketplace, no separate version string, and no second release step, used for `claude plugin eval` in CI and, if the skills are renamed, for `/joycraft:<name>` namespacing. Revisit a marketplace plugin only when (a) the P0-P11 rewrite has shipped and skill content has been stable for at least one quarter, per the 2026-03 deferral rule, and (b) either Joycraft is accepted into claude-plugins-official (the sole route to auto-update-on-by-default and install hints) or the manifest gains an ownership kind that records the plugin version alongside the CLI version so skew is detectable. Second qualification on hours: the five-to-two collapse saves little maintainer time by itself, because the per-harness cost lives in the 38 claude-gated blocks and the three fully forked skills, not in the three table rows and one test file that name the extra trees. The hours return only if the forks are cut too.

**On the human's position:** Section 10 has no direct P7 answer, so I engage the two answers that bear on distribution. Q3: "all I have to do is push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice." That sentence describes the CLI channel, not a plugin channel. Every skill already carries the update-check paragraph (scripts/lib/skill-template.mjs COMMON_UPDATE_ENTRY) and src/auto-safe-update.ts gates verified automatic updates; a third-party plugin does the opposite by default, since auto-update is off and users stay on the cached copy until the version string changes (host-marketplace.md, 'Release a new version'). Compound Engineering's README is the field report of what 'push and everyone gets it' looks like on a marketplace: it does not. My lens moves this position toward the CLI and against the plugin. Q2: "about 15 colleagues all of use it daily driver, across different size teams." Those teams share Joycraft by committing `.claude/skills` and `docs/templates` to git, which the 2026-03 research table already contrasted with the plugin model ('Each dev installs plugin', docs/features/plugin-architecture/research.md:41-47). A per-developer plugin puts the skill text on each laptop's update schedule while the templates, hooks, and check.mjs the skills cite 90 times stay on the repo's. Fifteen colleagues is exactly the population size where that skew shows up as 'the skill told me to open a template that is not there.' The human's wish for frictionless propagation is right; the plugin is the wrong instrument for it. If the human wants namespacing and eval Δ, both are available through a plugin.json inside the CLI-installed tree with no marketplace. If the human wants a second install channel for reach, `npx skills add` is free to me and already moves 28.5M installs a month; a marketplace is not free.

##### Team lead, five engineers — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P7 as written gives one team two version authorities. Codex engineers run the committed `.agents/skills` tree, pinned by git and recorded in `docs/.joycraft/manifest.json`; Claude engineers run a marketplace plugin cached per user under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/`. That cache (a) refreshes only if each engineer flips a per-user toggle, because "Background auto-update is off for your marketplace by default, and marketplace.json has no field to turn it on"; (b) is not fetched onto a teammate's machine by a committed `.claude/settings.json` ("Claude Code doesn't fetch it onto a machine where it isn't installed, unless its marketplace entry has a relative-path source"); (c) refreshes after "a random delay of up to ten minutes" and "the running session keeps the versions it loaded" until `/reload-plugins`; and (d) is pinned by the maintainer's `plugin.json` `version`, not by the team's repo. Meanwhile AGENTS.md, hooks, deny-patterns and templates still ride the CLI, so the provenance of one PR becomes (npm version × marketplace version × each engineer's reload state), and a branch from last month cannot reproduce the skill text that produced it. The 2026-03 deferral ("avoid iterating on two distribution formats") was a maintainer-hours argument; for a team it is a consistency argument, and it got stronger, not moot. The two benefits the proposition claims for the plugin do not need a marketplace: a skills-directory plugin committed under `.claude/skills/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` "is checked into the repository and reaches every collaborator who clones it", namespaces as `/joycraft:skill`, and is a valid `claude plugin eval` target (`name@skills-dir`). The third claimed benefit, install hints, is unavailable: "This page applies only if your plugin is listed in claude-plugins-official or another marketplace with one of Anthropic's official marketplace names." So the marketplace plugin adds a second, per-user, un-pinned distribution channel for a team and buys nothing the committed form does not.

**Qualification:** P7 holds only if "Claude plugin" means a skills-directory plugin that the CLI writes and commits under `.claude/skills/joycraft/` (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `skills/`), replacing the flat `.claude/skills/joycraft-*` tree rather than sitting beside it, and versioned by git together with `.agents/skills`, hooks, and AGENTS.md. A marketplace-distributed plugin may exist as a solo-user convenience but must not be the channel a team is told to use, and the two-dir tree must be tested for double-listing on hosts that read both dirs (Copilot dedupes; Cursor/Amp/OpenCode unverified). Drop "install hints" from the plugin's benefit list; they require the official marketplace.

**On the human's position:** Q3: "all I have to do is push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice." From my lens, "push" and "everyone" are the two words a marketplace plugin breaks. A third-party plugin is pull-only per user: auto-update is off unless each engineer toggles it, the update waits up to ten minutes into a session, the running session keeps the old copy until `/reload-plugins`, and a committed `.claude/settings.json` does not fetch it for a teammate unless the marketplace uses a relative-path source. The one channel that actually reaches everyone at once is the one Joycraft already has: one engineer runs `npx joycraft update`, opens a PR, the team reviews the diff of the skill text itself, merges, and every clone is on the same bytes. That is the CLI, not the plugin. So my lens moves Q3: "everyone gets the new juice" argues for the committed tree and against a marketplace plugin. Q2: "if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others... 15 colleagues... across different size teams." The marketplace plugin is exactly the path that works for one machine with one toggle and diverges for a team; the lead's "same path" reading of Q2 survives only if the plugin is the committed skills-directory form. Q4 ("gates that cannot be overridden"): a gate a Codex engineer hits and a Claude engineer does not, because the two run different skill versions, is a gate the team will learn to route around. P7 as written creates that split; the qualified form does not.

##### Solo dev on Pi, open-weight model — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P7 bundles four moves, and only two of them touch a Pi user. "No MCP main channel" and "keep the CLI" stand from my lens: Pi ships no MCP, and the 28.5M/month git installer writes only `.pi/skills` for Pi, with hooks for Claude Code and Kiro only, so it cannot carry the 594 lines of Pi-only runtime (`.pi/scripts/joycraft/*`, `.pi/agents/*`, the pipeline extension) or AGENTS.md. The other two moves fail as written. (1) "One skills tree to `.agents/skills`" ignores that Pi and Codex both read `.agents/skills` but need different prose: `scripts/lib/skill-template.mjs:11-46` gives Codex `$joycraft-` / Cmd+N and Pi `/skill:joycraft-` / `/new`, and the canonical skills carry 141 `{{skill_prefix}}`, 21 `{{clear}}` and 13 `{{skills_dir}}` sites. One tree means one rendering, so the Pi reader gets Codex instructions, the exact "silent failure" the 2026-06-11 single-source brief fixed for Codex desktop. (2) The Claude plugin is premature by the repo's own criterion: `docs/features/plugin-architecture/research.md:55` (2026-03-24) says "Package as plugin once feature set is stable to avoid iterating on two distribution formats," and the intent proposes reshaping all 22 skills. Worse for me, the plugin's headline benefit, eval Δ, runs only through `claude plugin eval` on a Claude model (`--model`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`); if that Δ gates the shared tree, skills get pruned against a frontier model while Lin et al. (2605.30621) and the harness ablation (2609.20804, +11.6% planning for a 30B model) say the open-weight user loses the scaffolding that helps them most. The maintainer's hours are the one shared resource; a second Claude-only channel spends them on the one harness that already has the most.

**Qualification:** P7 stands only under four conditions: (a) the two-dir tree ships with harness-neutral skill bodies (no `{{skill_prefix}}` / `{{clear}}` / `{{skills_dir}}` in prose; invocation and session-reset instructions move to a per-harness router line in AGENTS.md or a small per-harness header), or Pi keeps a `.pi/skills` variant that verifiably shadows `.agents/skills`; (b) the Pi runtime files (scripts, agents, pipeline extension) and AGENTS.md remain CLI-installed and the CLI remains the update channel for every harness; (c) the Claude plugin ships only after the P1 hub consolidation has landed, per the repo's own 2026-03-24 criterion ('once feature set is stable'), and its `claude plugin eval` Δ gates only Claude-specific content (never the shared tree) unless the shared tree is also evaluated under Pi on at least one open-weight model; (d) no MCP server as the main channel, which already holds for this lens. Absent (a) and (c), P7 as written degrades the Pi/open-weight path to fund a Claude-only one.

**On the human's position:** The maintainer's Q3 words are the load-bearing ones for P7: "all I have to do is push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice." From my lens that push channel already exists and is harness-neutral: every skill entry on every harness runs `docs/.joycraft/check.mjs` and can auto-apply a verified update (skill-template.mjs:108). A third-party Claude plugin is a worse push: auto-update is off by default and the live session keeps the old version until `/reload-plugins` (install.md, 2026-09-24), which is the exact stranding Compound Engineering warns about. So the plugin does not deliver "everyone gets the new juice"; the CLI does, and a Pi user on Qwen only ever receives it through the CLI. Q2, "Me truly first as I am the super user… about 15 colleagues all of use it daily driver, across different size teams," is the strongest case for the plugin, because the super-user runs Claude Code and gets namespacing and eval Δ. I attack it on his own second clause: fifteen daily drivers across harnesses is a fleet, and the only asset they all share is the CLI-installed tree plus AGENTS.md, which a plugin cannot carry. Adding a Claude-only channel now splits the one finite input, the maintainer's hours, away from that shared path. Q1 says the invariant is "gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed" and "getting people used to TDD agentic development"; that invariant is delivered on Pi by the scripts, the pipeline extension and the process prose, none of which a plugin or `npx skills add` moves, and all of which an eval Δ measured on Fable would tend to prune. My lens moves the position from "hybrid now" to: two dirs and CLI now with harness-neutral prose (or a shadowing Pi variant), plugin after the hub consolidation lands and only if its eval Δ never gates the shared tree, no MCP. It does not move Q5 or Q4, which are outside P7.

##### Evidence auditor — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** The plugin leg of P7 is proposed at the exact moment its own 2026-03 precondition fails, and two of the three benefits the pack credits to it do not hold for Joycraft. The deferral record (docs/research/plugin-architecture.md:51-55, commit 9aa8edd 2026-03-24) already designed this hybrid — "Both: Plugin provides skills globally. CLI still scaffolds per-project artifacts" — and deferred it "once feature set is stable to avoid iterating on two distribution formats." P1/P4/P8 propose to collapse 22 skills into a hub plus core, add forwarding shims, and generate skills per project: the skill set is about to be at its least stable, so shipping a marketplace plugin now recreates the two-format churn the record avoided. Of the benefits named ("namespacing, eval delta, install hints"): install hints require the plugin to be in `claude-plugins-official` or another Anthropic-named marketplace — the cli-hints page says it "applies only if your plugin is listed in claude-plugins-official or another marketplace with one of Anthropic's official marketplace names. The community marketplace, claude-community, isn't one of them" (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-hints.md, 2026-09-24); Joycraft at 453 downloads/month is not there. Namespacing is already solved by the `joycraft-` prefix (decision-log 2026-03-24) and a plugin would rename every command from `/joycraft-x` to `/joycraft:x`, a second migration for the 15 daily users. Auto-update is "off for every other marketplace" (loading.md) so a third-party plugin delivers updates only when each user toggles it or runs `/plugin marketplace update`, which is weaker than the CLI's existing per-conversation update offer. Separately, the "one skills tree to two dirs" leg hides two costs the pack does not state: (a) five surveyed harnesses read BOTH `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills` (Copilot, Cursor, omp, OpenCode, Amp), so every skill is listed twice unless the host dedupes by name — Pi documents "first discovered wins with a warning"; Copilot and Cursor docs state no rule (UNVERIFIED); (b) today's per-harness variants are not one tree: scripts/lib/skill-template.mjs:13-44 substitutes a different `skill_prefix` per harness (`/joycraft-`, `$joycraft-`, `/skill:joycraft-`) and a different `skills_dir`, and four skills carry real body forks (joycraft-implement-feature.md has 10 `<!-- harness: -->` blocks). One file in `.agents/skills` read by Codex, Pi, omp, Copilot and Cursor must be harness-neutral or it names the wrong invocation syntax on most of them. The evidence supports "CLI + two dirs, no MCP main channel"; it does not support adding a marketplace plugin now.

**Qualification:** P7 stands only under these conditions: (1) The Claude plugin leg is either a project-scope skills-directory plugin written by the CLI into `.claude/skills/` (one format, git-committed, verified `@skills-dir` loading), or a marketplace plugin deferred until the hub/core skill set from P1/P4/P8 has stabilized — the same condition the 2026-03 record set — with `version` omitted from plugin.json so users track commits. (2) 'Install hints' is dropped from the plugin's benefit list until Joycraft is accepted into `claude-plugins-official`; today the hint is official-marketplace-only. (3) 'One skills tree to two dirs' ships only after either verifying that Copilot, Cursor, omp, OpenCode and Amp dedupe same-named skills across `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, or writing a harness-neutral tree that drops per-harness `skill_prefix` and `skills_dir` substitutions and the four body-forked skills — and after the Pi install target is reconciled with Pi's documented `.agents/skills` location. (4) The 'no MCP main channel' clause needs no condition; it holds on verified evidence.

### P8 — Which skills die when process prose is cut

**Ruling: QUALIFY.** P8 does not stand as written. Its line counts are canonical source totals that bundle two or three per-harness bodies (installed: research 266 Claude / 186 elsewhere, verify 176/174, decompose 436/382, new-feature 509/504; whole tree 4,504 Claude / 4,276 Pi, not 5,573). Verify is not process prose: about 60% of its installed body is the oracle step, the read-only verifier prompt, and the report contract, i.e. the "independent verification" P8 says to keep. Research is already compact and its "process" is an information-flow constraint (brief isolation, capped Step 0 retrieval, Phase 4 reconciliation after a documented drift incident). No cited study measured removing static procedural prose from a frontier model; the harness ablation tested Nemotron-3 and Mistral-Medium, ablated a planning tool + protocol, and found that structure *saves* cost at the top tier. The vendor sentence P8 leans on is conditional ("if default performance is better"), and Joycraft has no eval that can satisfy that condition. What survives: new-feature (509, over Claude Code's own 500-line limit) and decompose (436) are genuinely long; the real bulk is duplicated ceremony (a ~45-60 line render block in 7 skills, three full research bodies), and SkillsBench's live revision says compact skills beat comprehensive ones. None of the four named skills "dies"; two get trimmed, two come off the cut list.

**Claim as argued:** Frontier models need less process scaffolding, so the step-by-step prose in research (626 lines), decompose (469), new-feature (516), verify (514), and others should be cut hard while independent verification, grounded progress claims, and persisted state are kept. Skeptic angles: the inverted-U says mid-tier and open-weight models still benefit; Joycraft serves Pi and omp users on such models; the harness ablation cost the strongest model only 0.4 to 2.0 points, a small penalty for keeping structure; Anthropic still recommends checklists for unattended Opus 5.5 runs.

**Replacement claim:** None of research, decompose, new-feature, or verify dies when process prose is cut. Trim new-feature and decompose (the only two that are long as installed), delete cross-skill ceremony duplication everywhere, keep verify whole and research's isolation/retrieval/reconciliation protocol, exempt the novice-protecting question discipline, and gate every remaining protocol cut on a per-model-class eval that Joycraft does not yet have.

**Condition:** P8 holds only as: (1) restated against installed per-harness variants, with research and verify removed from the cut list and verify's oracle/verifier/report plus research's isolation rule, Step 0 caps, and Phase 4 reconciliation classed as verification structure; (2) the first cut is ceremony and duplication, not protocol: the repeated HTML-render block, "Recommended Next Steps" menus, "Why:" narration, and the three research/verify harness bodies that differ only by subagent mechanics; (3) the human-facing question-discipline prose in new-feature (forced choice, >=2 real options, defer-to-name, ten-line chat cap) is exempt or kept inline as one short paragraph, never a pointer, per the repo's own 2026-07-29 observation; (4) any cut to protocol prose in new-feature or decompose ships behind a with/without eval (claude plugin eval or a pi -p equivalent) on every model class the one path serves, including at least one Pi/omp open-weight configuration, kept only where the delta is non-negative on all of them; (5) the static prose remains the offline default in the Pi/omp tree because no open-weight vendor publishes a prompting guide to fetch and subtract from.

**Judge's reasoning:** Four skeptics from four lenses converged on "qualified" for independent reasons, and I verified the load-bearing facts myself rather than taking either side's word. (a) Counts: wc on src/skills vs the five generated trees confirms the 626/514/469/516 figures include multiple harness bodies (markers at joycraft-research.md:11,269,448 and joycraft-verify.md:12,179,348); the model a user runs sees at most 266/176/436/509. Research is overstated 2.4x, verify 2.9x; the tree total is overstated by 19-23%. (b) Composition: installed Claude verify headings put Step 2.5 oracle gathering at 33-49, the verifier subagent prompt at 63-127, the report contract at 127-158; that is the verification P8 keeps, so verify cannot be a cut target without contradicting P8's own second clause. Research's remaining prose is the "must never see the brief" rule, a capped retrieval step, and Phase 4 reconciliation; capability does not remove the need for isolation. (c) Evidence: my WebFetch of arXiv 2609.20804 confirms the models are Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B and Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B, "planning" is an update_plan tool plus system protocol with no mention of skills or procedural files, and enabling planning cut cost ~30% (550B) and ~32% (Mistral) with -2.0/-0.4pp accuracy. The skeptic angle in the proposition ("a small penalty for keeping structure") therefore inverts the paper: at the top tier, structure is a cost saver. The paper's mechanism ("reducing redundant post-edit verification") is also about stopping behavior, not about following fewer steps. Lin et al. shows strong tier still gains (+2.6/+2.8pp), less than mid-tier (+15.8/+19.3), so "benefit less" was read as "harm". Anthropic's Fable 5 sentence is explicitly conditional on measurement, and the Opus 5.5 guide says Opus 5 prompts "should perform well without changes". (d) Joycraft has no eval that can satisfy that condition (§8.6, skill-evals brief DRAFT). CE's ce-retune refuses to retune without an A/B harness; P8 asks Joycraft to retune with none. (e) What survives is real: SkillsBench live says compact/standard skills (+19.0/+21.5) beat detailed (+14.5) and comprehensive (+0.7); Claude Code docs say under 500 lines and "state what to do rather than narrating how or why"; new-feature at 509 breaks the first, decompose's Why blocks break the second; the render block repeats in 7 skills and Decide-first in 5. That licenses trimming and deduplication now, without an eval. (f) The open-weight audience is not hypothetical: AGENTS.md dispatches Pi on kimi-k3, and the Pi tree is already the shortest, so Joycraft ships no extra scaffolding for weaker models today; a further cut lands on the tier the only skills-directory study says benefits 6-7x more than frontier. (g) Two lenses add a fact the others missed: the novice's killers are the gates P8 keeps, not the prose it cuts, and the brief already captures "User expertise" with zero consumers (grep confirmed); the solo-pi lens shows verify on Pi depends on a `subagent` tool that stock Pi lacks and that Joycraft's pipeline extension does not register (grep confirmed), so the pillar P8 wants kept is the least guaranteed one on Pi. Neither changes the ruling but both belong in the record as conditions on P3/P9/P11.

**Strongest refutation considered:** The strongest case for keeping P8 as written: the field is already moving this way (Superpowers deleted stubs and its Codex hook; Agent OS v3 removed spec writing and orchestration), Anthropic says a brief instruction now steers behaviors that used to need enumeration and that prior-model skills "can degrade output quality", SkillsBench measures length hurting (comprehensive +0.7 vs compact +19.0), and the harness ablation shows planning's accuracy value vanishing above 30B. If these are combined, "cut hard, keep verification" is the natural reading, and the line-count quibble is a detail about which file was counted. I rejected it on three grounds: none of those sources measured static hand-written procedural prose on any model, let alone a frontier one (the ablation is a tool+protocol on Nemotron/Mistral; SkillsBench measures module count and length classes, not step structure; the vendor claims are hedged and conditional on measurement); the only cost datum runs the other way at the top tier; and the counting error is not a detail, because it changes which skills are candidates at all (verify and research drop out) and how much cutting is even possible on the trees users run. The field precedents report no measured delta, and Anthropic's own skill-creator post says "Evals tell you when that's happened."

Two of three put GPT-OSS-120B mid-tier, and Qwen3-235B (open-weight, the largest gain) is mid-tier on every reading, so the auditor's conclusion that open-weight equals weak tier overreaches; open-weight models span both tiers.

**What would change the ruling:** Flip to keep (cut hard) if a with/without eval on the installed skills, run on Fable 5.1 or Opus 5.5 and on at least one Pi/omp open-weight configuration (Qwen3-235B or kimi-k3 class), shows a non-negative pass-rate or verifier-score delta after removing research's Step 0/isolation/Phase 4 prose and verify's oracle step; that would prove those blocks are dead weight on every tier the one path serves. Flip to a harder keep-the-prose ruling if the same eval shows a measurable loss on the open-weight configuration, or if a study appears that ablates static procedural SKILL.md prose (not a planning tool) on a frontier model and finds harm. Weaken condition (5) if joycraft telemetry shows Pi/omp users overwhelmingly run frontier closed models via API rather than open-weight ones. Drop the novice exemption if P11 rules Levels 1-2 out of scope and Q2's one path is confirmed as practitioners only.

**Human position moved?** Q1 (process prose generated) moved by all four skeptics, in one direction. The generated half has the weakest live evidence in the pack: SkillsBench's current revision puts self-generated skills 8.1-11.3pp below the no-skill baseline on frontier configurations, Lin et al. shows even Opus 4.6's evolved skills gain only +2.6pp, and every study where generation helped had a held-out verifier that a solo dev on a BYO key does not have. The panel moves Q1 from 'generated' to 'curated, shortened, eval-gated static default; generated prose only behind an acceptance gate, and never the sole copy in the Pi/omp tree.' The invariant half (gates, lifecycle, artifacts, STE, TDD) is not contradicted by any citation; but the auditor shows 'the formality of the loop' is not separable from 'process prose' in the current files (decompose's 3-7 specs / <=2 dependencies rules, verify's 70-line verifier prompt), so the human must name which lines are formality before anyone can cut the rest. Q3 (push the new prompting guide and everyone gets the new juice) moved: the guide's own removal advice is conditional on 'if default performance is better', Claude Code and Codex already inject per-model guidance, and no open-weight vendor publishes a guide, so 'everyone' means Claude and OpenAI users; a Pi/Qwen/Kimi user gets nothing from the fetch path and would lose prose if P8 cut it in the same release. Q4 (gates that cannot be overridden) not moved but sharpened by two lenses: the ai-researcher notes the recent unshippable slop occurred on Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1 with today's prose intact, so cutting prose does not address the gap the human named and verification does, which favors keeping verify whole; the novice warns an unoverridable INVENTED gate in front of a Level 1-2 user is an abandonment unless the gate carries a pre-picked recommendation and a 'pick for me' answer. Q2 (one path, maintainer first) not moved, but it binds P8: the maintainer's own AGENTS.md dispatches Pi on kimi-k3, so any cut on one path lands on the open-weight tier too.

#### Skeptics

##### Solo dev on Pi, open-weight model — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P8 argues from numbers no model ever reads and from studies that measure something other than skill prose. The "626-line research" and "514-line verify" figures are source files holding three full harness bodies each (src/skills/joycraft-research.md:11,269,448; joycraft-verify.md:12,179,348); the Pi user is served 186 lines (~2.5k tokens) of research and 174 of verify (.pi/skills/*/SKILL.md), both under Claude Code's own 500-line guidance. Only new-feature (504) and decompose (382) are actually long, and in each roughly 60 lines are the same HTML-render ceremony block repeated across six skills (Render and open at .pi/skills/joycraft-research/SKILL.md:104-166, decompose:106-168, new-feature:234-292, design:199-290). Meanwhile the one study that measures benefit from skills-directory content puts my model class at the peak: Qwen3-235B gains +19.3pp on SWE from updated skills versus +2.6pp for Claude Opus 4.6 (arxiv 2605.30621, Table 1, fetched 2026-09-24), and Joycraft's own dogfood profile dispatches Pi on kimi-k3 (AGENTS.md:182). The ablation paper the pack calls "frontier" evidence tested only Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B and Mistral-Medium — open-weight models — and measured a planning phase, not SKILL.md prose; planning already gave no gain at 120B (arxiv 2609.20804, fetched 2026-09-24). So the two studies disagree about the 200B-1T open-weight class and neither measures the thing P8 wants to cut. Joycraft has zero skill evals on any model (evidence pack §8.6). A hard cut on the Pi tree is therefore a guess, and the guess is made against the tier the only relevant study says benefits most.

**Qualification:** Cut is safe for this lens only under three conditions. (1) Cut the ceremony, not the protocol: remove the repeated HTML-render blocks, the 'Recommended Next Steps' menus, and the duplicated 'Decide first' paragraphs from every tree (they are handoff-through-human and UI, not scaffolding), but keep the bounded-protocol prose — retrieval caps (3-6 terms, at most 5 files), the isolation subagent prompts, output-path and 'Prior knowledge reused' contracts, and the Phase 4 reconciliation table — in the Pi/omp tree until a mid-tier eval shows they are dead weight. (2) Measure before cutting on Pi: run at least one invocation eval per cut skill on a Qwen3-235B-class model with a BYO key (Joycraft has none today, §8.6); the ablation's 120B null result and the inverted-U's 235B peak conflict for this class, so no cut can be justified from the literature alone. (3) Keep the static prose as the offline, vendor-less default: fetch-and-subtract profiles do not exist for open-weight vendors, so the Pi tree's prose is the only model guidance those users get and must not depend on a network or a Claude-only guide. Also restate the proposition against installed sizes: only new-feature (504) and decompose (382) exceed 300 lines on Pi; research and verify are already compact and should not be named as cut targets.

**On the human's position:** Q1: "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated." From my lens the generated half has no gate: SkillsBench says self-generated skills give no benefit on average and every study where generation helped had a held-out verifier, and a solo dev on Pi has no held-out task set to be that verifier. The inverted-U does say my model can write updates as good as Opus 4.6's, so generation quality is not the objection — the absence of an acceptance gate for one person on one key is. My lens moves Q1 to: generated prose may exist, but a maintainer-curated static default must ship in the Pi tree and remain the fallback when nothing is generated or accepted. Q3: "push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice." There is no juice for me: r6.2 found no prompting guide from any open-weight vendor, and Codex/Claude Code already inject their own. 'Everyone' in that sentence means Claude and OpenAI users; a Pi/Qwen/Kimi user gets nothing from the fetch path and loses prose if P8 cuts it in the same release. My lens qualifies Q3 to Claude/OpenAI harnesses only. Q4: "Gates that cannot be overridden." I do not fight this — Pi `tool_call` extension hooks can block (evidence pack §7 table), and blocking gates are cheaper for me than prose a mid-tier model follows unevenly. The human's frame is implicitly a Claude Code frame; nothing in Q1-Q4 names the open-weight path the maintainer's own AGENTS.md:182 dispatches to.

##### Evidence auditor — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P8 rests on numbers that are misread and on studies that do not test its premise. (1) The line counts are canonical source files that embed two or three full per-harness bodies. Installed, what a model reads is: research 266 lines on Claude / 186 on Pi, Codex, omp, Copilot (not 626); verify 176 / 174 (not 514); decompose 436 / 382; new-feature 509 / 504 (src/claude-skills/, src/pi-skills/, wc -l 2026-09-24). Research is overstated 2.4x, verify 2.9x. Of verify's 176 installed lines, ~70 are the read-only verifier-subagent prompt (src/claude-skills/joycraft-verify.md:64-127), which is the "independent verification" the proposition says to keep; verify is not process prose. (2) No cited study measures static hand-written process prose on a frontier Claude or GPT-6 model. The harness ablation (arXiv 2609.20804) tests Nemotron-3 30B/120B/550B and Mistral-Medium-3.5; its "strongest" is a 550B Nemotron. And its cost figure runs the other way from the skeptic angle: for the 550B model, enabling planning cut cost ~30-32% with -2.0/-0.4pp accuracy, so keeping the planning scaffold is net cheaper, not "a small penalty." Lin et al. (2605.30621) measures benefit from self-evolved harness updates, not static prose; its weak tier is the open-weight models (Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-120B) and they "gain little," so the inverted-U does not protect open-weight Pi/omp users the way the angle claims. (3) SkillsBench (2602.12670), cited from a stale revision, in its live June 2026 version still shows curated skills adding +18.2 to +24.8pp on Claude Code + Opus 4.7, Codex + GPT-5.5, and Gemini CLI + Gemini 3.1 Pro, and self-generated skills landing 8.1 to 11.3pp BELOW the no-skill baseline. The one live datum that supports cutting is the same paper's "compact and standard-length Skills (+19.0, +21.5pp) outperform detailed (+14.5) and comprehensive documentation (+0.7)", which argues for shorter, de-narrated skills, not for removing step structure because frontier models no longer need it. Anthropic's own sentence is conditional: "Review and consider removing older instructions if default performance is better" (Fable 5 guide, fetched 2026-09-24). The evidence supports shorten-and-measure, not "cut hard."

**Qualification:** P8 stands only under three conditions. (1) It is re-stated against installed variants (research 266/186, verify 176/174, decompose 436/382, new-feature 509/504), not canonical source; the source-level duplication is a maintainer cost, not a model-facing one, and belongs to a different proposition. (2) verify is removed from the cut list and research's Step 0 retrieval and question/fact isolation (src/claude-skills/joycraft-research.md:16-32, 78-82) are classed as verification structure, not process prose. (3) Every cut ships behind a with/without eval on the actual harness + model pairs Joycraft serves, including at least one Pi or omp open-weight configuration, in the SkillsBench pattern; the only live evidence for cutting is 'compact beats comprehensive' plus a vendor sentence conditioned on 'if default performance is better.' What the evidence does license now, without an eval: trim new-feature under the documented 500-line limit and remove 'Why:' narration per 'state what to do rather than narrating how or why.'

**On the human's position:** Q1: \"biggest wins in addition is the STE (Simplified Technical English) language directive, the formality of the loop, getting people used to TDD agentic development\" with the choice \"Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated.\" Two audit problems. First, \"formality of the loop\" and \"process prose\" are not separable in the files: decompose's loop formality is its step rules (3-7 specs, one-sentence descriptions, ≤2 dependencies, src/claude-skills/joycraft-decompose.md:77-90) and verify's is a 70-line verifier prompt. Cutting prose hard while keeping formality is not a choice the current files permit without naming which lines are which. Second, \"process prose generated\" is the one configuration with measured harm in the live evidence: SkillsBench's current revision puts self-generated skills 8.1 to 11.3pp below the no-skill baseline on Claude Code + Opus 4.7 and Codex + GPT-5.5, worse than the pack's \"no benefit on average.\" My lens moves \"generated\" to \"curated, shortened, and eval-gated\"; it does not move the invariant (gates, artifacts, STE, TDD), which no citation contradicts. Q3: \"push the new prompting guide to an update and everyone gets the new juice\" skips the condition the guide itself attaches, \"if default performance is better\", and the skill-creator post's \"Evals tell you when that's happened.\" The vendor asks for a measurement before removal; a push without one is the same untested prior the proposition rests on.


### P9 — Front-loaded quality at the design bookend

**Ruling: QUALIFY.** P9 stands only in its subtractive, human-declared form: a readiness state the human declares (never the agent infers) that keeps exploration in chat and renders the checkpoint once the human says the idea is clear; a first-class "I don't know yet / explore this" escape in the existing checkpoint that records an open row with an owner and returns to chat, never auto-routing to a panel; and visuals (mockups for frontend, inline diagrams for complex API/database work) drawn inside the existing design and review-gate renders under the one-template rule, tiered by the human-approved risk judgment that already exists. Panels as a standard per-feature step, new diagram or prototype templates, and any agent-side clarity detector do not stand: they have zero external evidence, zero cost measurement, zero skill mechanism, and their one external anchor (Helix) does not describe them.

**Claim as argued:** Panels while exploring, checkpoint artifacts once the idea is clear (switch on clarity, not on skill boundary; "I do not know yet" as a valid answer), diagrams and prototypes before specs, all tiered by risk, so spec and implementation tokens land on what the human wants. The maintainer runs panels and prototypes by hand today and reports it works. Skeptic angles: cost of a panel per feature; artifact fatigue (the reading-fatigue verdict was delete, tier, verify); prototype and spec drift; how the agent detects clarity; whether a novice can use any of it.

**Replacement claim:** Front-load quality at the design bookend by switching surface on human-declared clarity, not on skill boundary: chat (and hand-run panels, at the human's call) while exploring; the existing checkpoint, with an "I don't know yet" escape that records an owned open row, once the human declares the idea clear; visuals inside the existing gate renders, tiered by the human-approved risk judgment. Panels, diagram templates and prototypes remain human-decided practice, not shipped standard steps, until a panel's cost is measured and the checkpoint works on every harness.

**Condition:** P9 holds when all of the following are true: (a) clarity is a human-declared state ("still exploring" vs "ready to decide"), added as one sentence to the shared question directive in the eight gate skills, identical across harnesses; while the human says they are exploring, stay in chat and render no checkpoint; no agent-side inference. (b) The checkpoint gains a fourth escape (`__explore`) that leaves the question `open` with an owner (default the answerer) and a revisit gate, returns to chat, and never auto-routes to a panel; this touches CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html, interactive-checkpoint.md, decide.md's terminal states, the five PRE_PRESENTATION skills and gate-contract tests once. (c) The dossier pilot's kill criterion is adjudicated on the record before anything is called standard: count bypasses since 2026-07-20 and stamp the re-reading "bypass while exploring is expected; bypass once declared clear kills the format". (d) Visuals stay inside existing renders (design.html, review-gate, checkpoint) as inline SVG or mockup under D1's one-template rule; mockups for frontend features are the first visual, sequence/data-flow diagrams only when the existing human-approved risk judgment marks the feature complex. Excluded until preconditions are met: panels as a per-feature step (preconditions: token and hour cost measured on at least two features, one before/after on rework or parked-after-approval), new diagram/prototype templates and any prototype without a reconciliation step to the spec (precondition: the non-Claude checkpoint server ships so ceremony is not paste-back on four harnesses), automated risk tiering beyond the existing human-approved mode heuristic.

**Judge's reasoning:** All four skeptics returned "qualified"; none argued keep or flip, and their qualifications overlap on the core. What is repo-verified and uncontested: interview.md:39 and :44 force a checkpoint page for any gate with two or more questions with no clarity condition, on every harness; the escape set is __backlog/__discard/__defer only (CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html:264-268, interactive-checkpoint.md:31); the read-back already knows an `open` state for unanswered questions, so a fourth escape is a small extension, not new machinery. The timing defect the maintainer names is therefore real and cheap to fix, and it sits inside the reading-fatigue verdict rather than against it: RF-DIET-3 endorses a decision-forcing checkpoint at design and RF-DIET-2 says a doc enters the human channel only if it requires a decision. That is why this is not a flip.

What does not survive: the additive half. (1) Panels: zero hits for "panel" in src/skills; no token or hour cost recorded for any panel run (3, 13, 52, ~50 agents); Helix, verified live, has no pre-code design, diagram, prototype or panel phase — the engineer approves a checkpoint sequence "in minutes" and then reviews "the code and running app", so it supports early feedback on working code (Q4/P3), not pre-spec ceremony. (2) Prototypes/diagrams as templates: succinct-gates D1 (decision-log:70) chose one generic template because per-gate templates multiply render checks; install-manifest.ts:30 has no ownership kind for agent-generated files. (3) Agent-detected clarity: no eval, no check, no precedent; decision-log 2026-05-30 kept mode selection human-approved because "only a human knows" risk. (4) The existing front-loaded gate is already skipped: 60 folders, 47 briefs, 10 design.md, 13 of 23 spec'd features with no design.md; one committed checkpoint render; and the Opus 5.5 feature went through two checkpoints, brief approval (D9) and nine specs and was parked the same day (2026-09-24, commits a9565e0/1d30997). That last fact cuts both ways: implementation tokens were saved, spec tokens were not; it is weak evidence for the bookend and strong evidence that more pre-spec artifacts do not by themselves make spec tokens land.

The Deposition Checkpoint pilot's kill criterion ("kill the format if Max bypasses the questions into free chat by the second feature", decision-dossier brief.md:88-90) was never adjudicated: decision-log 2026-09-23 C3 extended checkpoints to all eight gate skills, but no row records the pilot surviving. The evidence pack's own origin line is a bypass. The maintainer's clarification resolves the contradiction only if the criterion is re-read on the record as "bypass while exploring is expected; bypass once declared clear kills the format". That re-reading is a condition of this ruling, not an assumption.

On Q2's transfer claim ("if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others"): the checkpoint the maintainer calls amazing is the db-published Claude page; on Codex, Pi, omp and Copilot it is a paste-back block (interactive-checkpoint.md local mode; backlog 2026-09-23), which is RF-KILL-6. The team-lead and maintainer lenses are right that the super-user's experience does not transfer until the local server ships, so every added ceremony lands on four harnesses as a killed pattern.

**Strongest refutation considered:** The evidence-auditor's: P9 has no external evidence, its one anchor (Helix) is misread, the existing design gate is skipped in 13 of 23 spec'd features, the only fully front-loaded feature (Opus 5.5) was parked the day it was approved, and the Q4 slop sessions happened with design, decide and checkpoint already shipped, so the existing front-loaded gates did not prevent the failure the maintainer wants fixed. I verified Helix live and the auditor is right: the engineer approves a checkpoint sequence "in minutes" and reviews "the code and running app"; there is no pre-code design, diagram, prototype or panel step. This kills the additive half of P9 and reassigns the Q4 motive to P3 (blocking gates in the implement loop). It does not flip P9 because the timing defect is repo-verified (interview.md:39,44; three fixed escapes), the reading-fatigue verdict itself endorses a decision-forcing design checkpoint (RF-DIET-3), and the stated first customer (Q2) reports the clear-idea checkpoint works, with nine decisions stamped through one page in a day. The Opus 5.5 parking is also ambiguous: it wasted spec tokens but saved implementation tokens, which is half of what P9 promises.
