**Skeptic disagreements:**
- Destination of 'I don't know yet': novice says chat or another prototype iteration and never a panel; team-lead says never chat because chat has no owner, make it a committed open row with owner and revisit gate (extending __defer); maintainer says an 'explore' escape that leaves the question open and returns to chat; evidence-auditor names the escape but no destination. Ruling adopts the team-lead's owned open row with the maintainer's return-to-chat, and the novice's ban on auto-routing to a panel.
- Who signals clarity: team-lead says a human-declared state recorded in the gate, never inferred; maintainer says the human, not the agent; novice says a novice cannot declare clarity and the only working signal is a reaction to a prototype; evidence-auditor cites the Fable 5 guide ('pause only when the work requires them') without a mechanism. All four reject agent inference; they differ on whether a novice can declare at all.
- Diagrams: novice says sequence and data-flow diagrams do not survive for Level 1-2 users and belong behind the P11 fork; evidence-auditor accepts risk-tiered diagrams inside the existing design gate; maintainer allows inline SVG in existing renders only, under D1's one-template rule; team-lead wants them opted in per risk tier by a committed AGENTS.md policy line.
- Prototypes: novice says a clickable mockup is the one P9 surface that survives and should be the first artifact a novice meets; maintainer excludes prototype templates entirely until the non-Claude server ships and a panel cost exists; team-lead accepts throwaway prototypes only with a reconciliation step to the spec like design Step 3; evidence-auditor puts them in a pilot with instrumentation.
- Helix citation: novice, team-lead and maintainer mark it 'holds' (quotes verbatim, with the team-lead and maintainer noting the extension to pre-spec artifacts is a stretch); evidence-auditor marks it 'misread'. Judge's live check agrees with the auditor: the text holds, the use as support for pre-spec design artifacts does not.
- Panels' path to standard: novice gates them behind P11 or explicit request; team-lead wants one team feature's panel priced in tokens and hours and a per-tier AGENTS.md policy; maintainer keeps them hand-run and human-decided until cost is measured on two features; evidence-auditor demands a pilot with bypass/skip telemetry, per-panel token cost and a before/after. All agree they are not standard today.
- The bypass-to-chat kill criterion: maintainer re-reads it as 'bypass while unclear is expected; bypass once clear kills' and wants it stamped; evidence-auditor says the brainstorm-mode 'hindrance' is the July kill signal reframed after an uninstrumented graduation; team-lead wants bypasses counted before any re-reading; novice notes the super-user bypassed in the very session that produced P9.
- Feature-folder count since 2026-07-20: team-lead reports 13; the judge's glob over 2026-07/08/09 returns 15 (includes early-July folders). Not material to the ruling.
- Whether P9 is even about its stated first customer: novice says the proposition is out of scope for Q2's maintainer-first frame and only constrains shape; team-lead says Q2's 'works for me then for others' is exactly the transfer that fails on a mixed-harness team.

**Citation problems:**
- Shopify Helix (shopify.engineering/helix): every quoted sentence holds verbatim, but its use in section 9 item 8 as support for pre-spec panels/diagrams/prototypes is a misread. Verified live by the judge: the only pre-code human step is approving a checkpoint sequence 'in minutes'; the engineer then reviews 'the code and running app'. Helix supports P3/Q4 (gates on implemented checkpoints), not P9's design-bookend ceremony. Three skeptics marked it 'holds'; the evidence-auditor's 'misread' is correct.
- docs/guides/levels.md:24 'Most developers plateau at Level 2' misreads Dan Shapiro's five-levels post, which says 'almost everyone tops out here' about Level 3 (novice lens, live fetch 2026-09-24). Not a direct P9 citation but it anchors the novice framing.
- arXiv 2609.00252 cited as 'no controlled study of spec-driven development exists': directionally right, wording overstated; the paper says the evidence base is immature and is a conceptual first step; the words 'controlled', 'empirical', 'experiment' do not appear (evidence-auditor).
- Skill-creator post: the pack-implied URL claude.com/blog/skill-creator returns 404; the live post is claude.com/blog/improving-skill-creator-test-measure-and-refine-agent-skills (2026-03-03); substance holds as paraphrase (evidence-auditor).
- Agent OS v3.0.0 release year: pack says 2026-01-20; a fetch summary printed 2025; day/month match, year unverified (evidence-auditor).
- P9 paraphrases the reading-fatigue verdict as 'ask the human for decisions instead of reading'; the source reads 'demand decisions instead of reading' and 'kill if you bypass to chat'. Holds in substance.
- Team-lead's tally '13 feature folders since 2026-07-20': the judge's glob over 2026-07/08/09 returns 15 (includes early-July folders). Immaterial.

**What would change the ruling:** Toward keep (panels and prototypes as standard, risk-tiered steps): a recorded token and wall-clock cost for a panel on at least two features; a before/after showing that features that passed a panel or prototype had lower rework or fewer parked-after-approval outcomes than features that did not; the non-Claude checkpoint server shipped so the deciding surface is the same on every harness; and telemetry showing the clarity-declared checkpoint is completed, not bypassed, once the human declares clarity. Toward flip (drop the design-bookend additions and move the effort to P3): telemetry showing checkpoints are still bypassed after the clarity switch ships, or the `__explore` escape used as a permanent dodge on most questions, or the design-gate skip rate staying near 13 of 23 after the change; or a controlled study finding that upfront design artifacts do not reduce agent rework. A vendor or independent measurement that an agent can detect idea clarity reliably would reopen the agent-inference half that this ruling excludes.

**Human position moved?** Yes, on four of the five positions, with evidence. (1) The P9 clarification's 'switch on clarity' is strengthened but reshaped: all four skeptics converge that the human declares clarity and the agent never infers it; the clarification's 'human or the agent signals' loses its agent half because no eval, check or precedent exists (evidence pack line 211; decision-log 2026-05-30 'only a human knows'). The maintainer's own behavior supports the human-declared version: Q8 ('no brief though, as you and I will have follow up discussion') and the pack's chat-only origin are consistent with a person who knows when he is exploring. (2) 'I don't know yet routes back to chat or to a panel' is moved: routing an unclear answer to a panel is rejected by the novice (a 41-53 KB adversarial document is unreadable for that user) and by the maintainer lens (no panel mechanism, no cost); routing to chat alone is rejected by the team-lead (chat has no owner, and the repo already solved this with defer-to-person D2/D11). The panel converges on an owned open row that returns to chat. (3) 'Panels as a standard step' is moved to not-standard: zero cost figures across 3-, 13-, 52- and ~50-agent panels, zero skill mechanism, Helix misread (verified live: no pre-code panel), and the Opus 5.5 feature approved and parked the same day after full front-loading. The maintainer's hand-run practice stays exactly as it is; the panel denies only that it should ship as ceremony. (4) 'More visuals' is split: component mockups and prototypes survive as the one surface that needs no reading (novice, Helix's early-feedback principle applied to something a person can look at), but sequence and data-flow diagrams stay inside existing renders under D1's one-template rule and behind the risk judgment; new templates and untethered prototypes fail on drift (design.md:185-192) and on the manifest gap (install-manifest.ts:30). (5) Q2's 'if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others' is moved for the checkpoint specifically: the 'amazing' page is the Claude db-published page; on Codex, Pi, omp and Copilot it is paste-back (RF-KILL-6), so the transfer waits on the backlogged server. Not moved: Q1 (formality of the loop, TDD as the core objective) — every skeptic keeps the decision-forcing checkpoint at design, and RF-DIET-3 endorses it. Reframed: Q4's slop gap ('hours of unshippable output') happened with design, decide and the checkpoint already shipped, so it is evidence for P3's implement-loop gates, Helix's actual mechanism, not for more design-bookend ceremony; P9 does not close the Q4 gap.

#### Skeptics

##### Novice vibe coder — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P9's own escape hatch routes the least capable user into the least usable surface. The proposition says "I do not know yet / explore this" should route "back to chat or to a panel" (evidence pack line 254). A panel in this repo produces 41-53 KB adversarial documents with citations (docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md 52,711 bytes; docs/research/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-brief.html 52,455 bytes; the checkpoint page itself 41,455 bytes) built by 8 research agents plus 7 skeptic lenses plus judges (pack line 10, lines 262-263) or a "13-agent panel" (docs/context/decision-log.md:36). A person who cannot read a diff cannot read that, and cannot judge whether the panel's verdict is right. So for me, "I don't know" leads to a wall of text, then to a checkpoint whose every question demands a typed "<choice> because <reason>" (src/skills/joycraft-interview.md:48-56; docs/templates/CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html:243) and whose only escapes are Backlog, Discard, or Defer to a named person (CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html:264-267; a solo novice has nobody to defer to, and an unnamed defer is refused, interview.md:57-60). Second, the reading-fatigue verdict P9 must clear was "delete nominal output, tier the channels, retrieve just-in-time, and demand decisions instead of reading" (reading-fatigue-brief.html:229); P9 adds three artifact classes (panel reports, diagrams, prototypes) before the spec even exists. Third, the Deposition Checkpoint pilot's kill criterion was "kill if you bypass to chat" (reading-fatigue-brief.html:486), and the super-user bypassed to chat in the very session that produced P9: "Origin: /joycraft-interview session (chat-only, no gate artifacts by request)" (pack line 6). If the maintainer opts out of the artifact when exploring, a novice never opens it. Fourth, "the agent detects clarity" has no measurement anywhere in the repo: there are no invocation or behavior evals and check.sh cannot even tell which skill ran (pack line 211), so a clarity gate ships as unmeasured prose, the very thing the synthesis says to cut (pack line 224). What survives my lens: prototypes and component mockups before specs. A novice can look at a screen and say "not like that"; that is the one P9 surface that needs no reading and no vocabulary, and Helix's "moves feedback to the earliest useful point" (live, shopify.engineering/helix, 2026-09-21) applies to it. Sequence and data-flow diagrams do not survive: a Level 1-2 person cannot read a sequence diagram any more than a diff.

**Qualification:** P9 stands for this lens only under this condition: the default surface while exploring is chat, the first artifact a novice meets is a clickable mockup or prototype (frontend) or a plain-language "here is what I think you want" page (backend), the checkpoint gains an "I don't know yet" escape that routes to chat or to another prototype iteration and never to a panel, and panels plus sequence/data-flow diagrams are gated behind the practitioner fork (P11) or an explicit request. Any version where panels and diagrams are "standard steps" for every user, or where the checkpoint still requires a typed rationale with only Backlog/Discard/Defer escapes, fails week-two retention for a Level 1-2 user. The proposition is also out of scope for its stated first customer (Q2: maintainer first), so this qualification constrains the shape of P9, not whether the maintainer should build it for himself.

**On the human's position:** The human's words: "the artifacts are not the problem — answering questions directly inside them is 'amazing' once the idea is clear"; "the switch should key on clarity, not on which skill is running"; "'I don't know yet / explore this' as a first-class answer ... that routes back to chat or to a panel"; "artifacts need more visuals — sequence and data-flow diagrams ... component mockups and prototypes" (pack line 254). And on the customer: "Me truly first as I am the super user ... 15 colleagues ... one path ... as this system gets much easier ... this becomes a non issue really" (Q2). From my lens: the clarity switch is right in direction but the human answered only half of it. Clarity is something the super-user can feel and signal; I cannot. I do not know whether my idea is clear until I see it, so for me the only working clarity signal is a prototype I react to, not a question I answer. "I don't know" as a first-class answer is the one change that stops me abandoning at the checkpoint, but only if it routes to chat or to a mockup, never to a panel, because a panel's output is the wall of text I cannot read. The diagram half of "more visuals" does not move for me at all: sequence diagrams are a practitioner surface (P10/P11 fork), and mockups are the novice surface. The "amazing" claim is real but it is the super-user's testimony about an artifact tuned for him after two months of pilots, and he himself ran this exploration chat-only, which is the exact kill criterion his own panel set. The Q2 frame ("one path", maintainer first) means my lens does not flip P9; the human has already said the novice is not the first customer. It does move P9's shape: if "one path" is serious, the path must default to chat-plus-mockup and unlock panels, diagrams, and rationale-required checkpoints only when the user or a P11 profile asks for them. As written, with panels and diagrams standard and the checkpoint's escapes unchanged, I am gone before week two, and "TDD agentic development as the core objective" (Q1) never gets a chance to teach me anything.

##### Team lead, five engineers — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** As a *standard* step for a five-developer team, P9 fails on consistency before it can deliver quality. (1) The artifact that "dialogues with the user" is two different products on a mixed team: on Claude the answers live in one developer's private artifact store and never in the file (docs/templates/reference/interactive-checkpoint.md:16); on Codex/Copilot/Pi the same gate is a local page whose answers the developer pastes back as a block (interactive-checkpoint.md:5, :46-50; docs/backlog/2026-09-23-checkpoint-non-claude-harnesses.md). Only the stamped `decisions:` rows reach the repo, so the design-bookend record is already per-developer, and P9 adds three more artifact kinds (panel verdicts, diagrams, prototypes) with no committed home or reconciliation. (2) "Switch on clarity" pushes the biggest source of variance into the least observable variable. Nothing in the repo detects clarity; every gate skill forces a checkpoint page at two or more questions regardless (src/skills/joycraft-interview.md:39,44; joycraft-design.md:125,132; joycraft-new-feature.md:61,68). Five engineers have five clarity thresholds: a junior signals "clear" early because they do not know what they do not know, a senior signals late; the lead cannot see either. The checkpoint template has no "I do not know" escape at all today, only `__backlog`, `__discard`, `__defer` (interactive-checkpoint.md:31; docs/templates/CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html:267), and routing an unknown "back to chat" would destroy the one thing a team record needs: an owner. (3) The format P9 extends already tripped its own kill criterion and nobody adjudicated it. The Deposition Checkpoint shipped as a pilot: "Kill the format if Max bypasses the questions into free chat by the second feature" (docs/features/2026-07-20-decision-dossier/brief.md:89-92; docs/features/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-panel/research.md:47-49). The evidence pack's own origin line is "chat-only, no gate artifacts by request" (docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md:5), the maintainer calls the artifact "a hindrance" in brainstorm mode (:254), and across 13 feature folders since 2026-07-20 there is exactly one rendered checkpoint, 7 dossiers, 6 design.md files and 4 briefs with zero `decisions:` rows (ls/grep tally, docs/features/). No pilot review exists in decision-log.md, shipped.md or discoveries/. Building diagrams and prototypes on top of an unadjudicated kill is how a team lead ends up normalizing five different ceremonies by hand. (4) Prototype/spec drift is unhandled. The design skill already needs a whole reconciliation step because brief and design silently diverged once ("11 clean / 9 dirty", joycraft-design.md:185-192). A pre-spec prototype is a third artifact with no such step; on a team, dev A's HTML mockup becomes the de facto spec dev B implements differently, and a novice ships the prototype. (5) Panel cost is unmeasured anywhere: Helix publishes no cost or adoption numbers (live check) and describes code-level checkpoints after design, not pre-spec panels or prototypes, so the pack's Helix quote supports "early feedback" but not this mechanism. Panel output is LLM prose, and RF-5 says polished LLM plans "invite acknowledgment, not scrutiny" (research.md RF-5); five persuasive verdicts per week is added review load for the lead, not less.

**Qualification:** P9 stands only under all of: (a) the clarity switch is a human-declared state ('still exploring' vs 'ready to decide') recorded in the gate, never inferred by the agent, and the same rule applies on every harness; (b) 'I do not know yet' becomes a committed `open` decision row with an owner and a revisit gate (extending the existing `__defer` escape), not a route back to private chat; (c) panels, diagrams and prototypes are opted into per risk tier by a per-project policy line the team commits in AGENTS.md, so five developers run the same ceremony for the same tier, and prototypes are throwaway with a reconciliation step to the spec like design Step 3, or are not shipped; (d) the decision-dossier pilot's kill criterion is adjudicated on the record first (count bypasses since 2026-07-20) and one team feature's panel is priced in tokens and hours before 'standard' is written anywhere.

**On the human's position:** The maintainer's words: "the artifacts are not the problem — answering questions directly inside them is 'amazing' once the idea is clear. The failure is timing… the switch should key on clarity, not on which skill is running," plus "'I don't know yet / explore this' as a first-class answer in every artifact question that routes back to chat or to a panel," and Q2: "if I can get it to work best for me, we can easily get it for others." Three attacks from this lens. First, "amazing" is the Claude super-user's experience with the db-published page; the colleague on Codex gets a localStorage page and a paste-back block (interactive-checkpoint.md:46-50), so "once the idea is clear" describes one harness's surface, not the team's. Second, "key on clarity" names the right variable and then leaves it to the agent or to whoever is at the keyboard; on a team the person who is unclear is often not the person answering (team-ready-gates: a PM collects answers from other teams), so the signal must be a declared, committed state, not an inference. Third, "routes back to chat" is the wrong destination for a team: chat is the one place no second developer can read. The repo already solved this once with defer-to-person (D2/D11), which turns an unknown into an owner and a visible line. Q2's "works for me, then for others" is the exact transfer this lens denies: the super-user's clarity threshold, prototype discipline and panel habit are personal, and the tally shows even the super-user applied the bookend to 6 of 13 features. My lens moves the position, not to rejection but to a condition: keep the clarity switch as a human-declared 'still exploring / ready to decide' state; make 'I do not know yet' a recorded `open` row with an owner and a revisit gate, never a route to chat; and make panels and prototypes a per-project tier policy the team commits in AGENTS.md, so all five engineers pay the same ceremony for the same risk tier.

##### Maintainer counting hours — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P9 as written buys three new product surfaces (a panel step, new visual artifact types, a clarity detector plus a fifth answer state) for a problem the repo's own record says to solve by subtraction, and it does so on the surface that already eats most of the maintainer's hours. (1) The kill criterion already fired. The Deposition Checkpoint shipped with "kill the format if Max bypasses the questions into free chat by the second feature" (docs/features/2026-07-20-decision-dossier/brief.md:89-91; RF mechanism 4 at docs/features/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-panel/research.md:47-49). No decision-log row ever records the pilot surviving (grep of docs/context/decision-log.md for dossier/pilot/kill returns none), the format propagated to user-facing skills anyway, and the evidence pack's own header records the bypass: "Origin: /joycraft-interview session (chat-only, no gate artifacts by request)" (docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md:5). P9's "I do not know yet routes back to chat" legitimizes the exact behavior the pilot named as its kill signal, without saying which of the two was wrong. (2) The design bookend is already where the hours go. Five of the ten releases from 0.7.0 to 0.7.11 (2026-07-21 to 2026-09-03, six weeks) were gate/artifact/output-style work (CHANGELOG.md:179-439); since 2026-07-01 there are 49 commits touching src/skills, 18 touching src/templates, 102 touching tests; gate machinery alone carries 1,686 test lines (tests/gate-contract.test.ts 830, interactive-checkpoint 254, review-gate-template 215, gate-slot-contract-placement 210, artifact-render-steps 177), and the gate-contract test pins exact skill counts ("covers exactly the five question-bearing skills", tests/gate-contract.test.ts:209; PRE_PRESENTATION_SKILLS :93-99), so every new gate skill or answer state edits at least five exact-count assertions, the checkpoint template (487 lines), the protocol doc, five harness trees via sync-skills, and a CHANGELOG line for the docs-sync gate. (3) Panels have no product mechanism at all (grep 'panel' in src/skills/*.md: zero hits) and the repo's panels ran at 3, 13, 52 and "roughly fifty Opus 5.5 agents" (docs/backlog/2026-09-23-checkpoint-non-claude-harnesses.md:9; decision-log.md:36; reading-fatigue research.md:5; docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-checkpoint.html:365). Making that a "standard step" per feature is a token bill nobody has measured, and the risk-tiering that would cap it has a precedent that says it cannot be automatic: decision-log 2026-05-30 kept the size-to-mode heuristic human-approved because "only a human knows" risk (decision-log.md:94). A human-decided, hand-run panel is what exists today for free. (4) Visuals: succinct-gates D1 deliberately chose one generic REVIEW_GATE template because "per-gate templates multiply the render-check surface for no structural gain" (decision-log.md:70); sequence/data-flow/mockup/prototype templates reverse that decision, and prototypes would be files outside every manifest kind (src/install-manifest.ts:30 has only vendor | create-once | config-patch), never cleaned, on a repo where the folder map is already never regenerated after first install (evidence pack 8.4). (5) The checkpoint P9 wants to gate on clarity only works on Claude; every other harness gets paste-back (backlog 2026-09-23-checkpoint-non-claude-harnesses.md:11), which is RF-KILL-6 "do not rebuild" (reading-fatigue research.md:62-63). The server that fixes it is itself deferred as "its own feature" (same backlog:17).

**Qualification:** P9 stands only in its subtractive form, on existing surfaces, with nothing new to sync or test: (a) one sentence added to the shared question-directive paragraph in the eight gate skills — while the human says they are still exploring, stay in chat and render no checkpoint; the human, not the agent, signals clarity; (b) one added escape key in the existing CHECKPOINT_TEMPLATE.html and interactive-checkpoint.md (an 'explore' escape that leaves the question open and returns to chat), which is a fifth terminal state and therefore touches decide.md, the five PRE_PRESENTATION skills, and the gate-contract tests once; (c) the dossier pilot's bypass-to-chat criterion is re-read as 'bypass while unclear is expected; bypass once clear kills the format' and is stamped in the decision log so the contradiction closes. Not in scope: a panel skill or panel step (panels stay hand-run and human-decided per feature, as today, until a token cost per panel is measured on at least two features); new diagram, mockup, or prototype templates (the agent may draw an inline SVG inside the existing design.html or review-gate render when it helps, under D1's one-template rule); any agent-side clarity detector; any 'risk tier' automation beyond the human-approved mode heuristic that already exists. Condition for revisiting the excluded pieces: the non-Claude checkpoint server ships first (otherwise every added ceremony lands on four harnesses as RF-KILL-6 paste-back), and one measured panel cost exists.

**Strongest refutation:** P9 has no external evidence behind it, and its one external anchor is misread. The lead cites Helix ("moves feedback to the earliest useful point") for front-loading design; the live article (shopify.engineering/helix, 2026-09-21) has no design, spec, diagram, prototype or panel phase before code — the engineer only approves a checkpoint *sequence*, then reviews "the code and running app" per small checkpoint, and "the reference is the spec." Helix front-loads verification of working code, not design artifacts; it is evidence against P9's shape, not for it. Every other P9 support is internal and self-reported: "panel" appears in zero of the 22 skills, "prototype"/"mockup" in none, "diagram" once (decide.md:135, optional); the checkpoint artifact the maintainer calls "amazing" has exactly one committed render on this branch (docs/features/2026-09-22-fable-native-sdlc-harness/checkpoint-decide.html) plus two on the parked branch, all from 2026-09-22..24 — roughly two days of use, n=1, no metric, and docs/.joycraft/telemetry.json records zero checkpoint, design.md, panel, or cost events. Adding panels and prototypes as standard steps on top of a design gate already skipped in 50 of 60 feature folders (10 have design.md; 13 of the 23 spec'd features skipped design entirely) is asking for more of the ceremony the evidence says gets skipped or rubber-stamped.

### P10 — Architecture-defense session as setup step and maturity gate

**Ruling: QUALIFY.** P10 is qualified. The practice survives (agent surfaces the architecture, human corrects, corrections are recorded), but the phrase "enforceable architecture record" does not: nothing in Joycraft can enforce or re-check a prose architecture record, and the claim's own cited precedent (Helix) runs in the opposite direction, with a human-designed architecture enforced by reviewers checking code. It stands only when each correction terminates as a machine check or a decision-log row that an independent verifier reads and re-derives, it is an opt-in maturity mode of the design bookend rather than a universal setup step, and it ships as a measured pilot.

**Claim as argued:** At setup and as the project matures, the agent proposes the architecture, defends it with code examples, explains each decision; the human corrects; the corrections become the enforceable architecture record (Helix: documented architecture makes adversarial review enforceable; the reading-fatigue "theory ledger"). Skeptic angles: the human is the only verifier of the corrections, so what re-checks them as code drifts; the context map is "hopeful disclosure" so does the record get read; cost on a mature codebase; duplication with design, decide, and dangerous-assumptions; teams where corrector and implementer differ.

**Replacement claim:** Not a flip; the qualified claim reads: an architecture-confirmation session, run as an opt-in mode of the design bookend on existing code, in which the agent extracts the architecture from code with file:line evidence and the human corrects it; each correction lands in the same commit as a machine check or an owner-stamped decision-log row that joycraft-verify reads as oracle input and re-derives on drift triggers; piloted with a measured delta before it becomes a default gate.

**Condition:** P10 holds only under all of the following: (1) FORM: every human correction terminates, in the same commit, as exactly one of (a) a machine check the project owns (a harden deny pattern where the rule is path/regex-shaped per src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:33-37, otherwise a CI dependency/lint/test check such as a dependency-cruiser rule) or (b) a decision-log row (Date, Decision, Why, Alternatives, Revisit When, plus owner) in docs/context/decision-log.md; a correction that fits neither is discarded, not recorded; no new standalone architecture document and no Context Map pointer is created. (2) READER: src/skills/joycraft-verify.md Step 2.5 is extended so the verifier's oracle includes those decision-log rows, and a fresh-context subagent re-derives the recorded architecture against code when an evidence trigger fires (a verify FINDING, folder-map drift reported by tune, or a NEVER_READ telemetry verdict), so the human is not the only verifier. (3) PLACEMENT: it is not a step on the universal setup path. Greenfield reduces to joycraft-design Sections 3 and 4, which already exist. On existing code it is an explicit opt-in project-scope mode of design/decide that extracts rules from code for the human to confirm (Helix's direction), with the token cost stated up front, honoring src/skills/joycraft-gather-context.md:27. (4) TEAMS: one named owner per repo runs the session and commits the record; other engineers' sessions read it as a constraint and file corrections through the same owner-stamped path, never re-proposing the architecture. (5) EVIDENCE: it ships as a pilot with a pre-committed before/after count (verify FINDINGS per feature, or the maintainer's own hours-of-unshippable-output) because the only supporting evidence today is one uncontrolled self-report.

**Judge's reasoning:** All four skeptics returned "qualified"; none argued the practice is worthless and none argued the claim stands as written, and the evidence supports that split. Against "keep": the word "enforceable" has no mechanism. harden.md:19-20 names permissions.deny and deny-patterns.txt as "the only two enforcement surfaces" and :33-40 classes semantic rules ("repositories go through the service layer") as ineligible prose; verify.md Step 2.5's oracle is brief Hard Constraints + decisions frontmatter + boundary file and never reads the decision log or any architecture doc; implement reads nothing under docs/context (grep empty); design's retrieval is a grep capped at 5 rows (design.md:19-27). So after the human corrects once, no reader on the implement path and no re-check exists, which is the proposition's own first skeptic angle, confirmed in the repo. The Helix citation, which I fetched, holds verbatim but is misapplied: the architecture was designed by humans ("a highly opinionated architecture we designed"), the document is a standard "so reviewers have a standard to enforce", enforcement is two context-isolated reviewer agents over code, and the page is silent on memory storage and on re-verifying documentation against code. P10 inverts the direction (agent proposes) and borrows the word "enforceable" without the reviewers. The repo also shows the drift failure in miniature: the folder map, a machine-derivable record, is regenerated only on create-once generation paths (agents-md.ts:148, improve-claude-md.ts:414) and AGENTS.md has no docs/intent row while the folder exists; a hand-corrected prose record would drift faster. The setup-step framing collides with gather-context.md:27's explicit no-code-scan cost rule and with the pack's own constraint that the practice "requires a CS background". Against "flip": the decision log survived a six-panelist trial 6/6 with an in-repo demonstration of reuse; Helix explicitly records reviewer feedback so autonomy grows; Anthropic's Fable guidance recommends recording corrections and fresh-context verifiers; the ETH study finds instructions in context files are followed even though success does not rise, so the failure mode is reads and drift, not compliance; and the escalation rule in add-fact.md:24 and session-end.md:64 already routes enforceable facts to harden, giving P10's outputs a legitimate home. The practice therefore has value under conditions the skeptics converge on: check-or-row form, a verifier reader, opt-in on existing code, one owner on teams, and a pilot. The five conditions above are the union of their qualifications where they agree and my resolution where they split (see skeptic_disagreements).

**Strongest refutation considered:** The harness-expert's combined argument: P10 produces the one artifact class the repo has already ruled unenforceable (harden.md:13 "Prose is a rule the model merely hopes to follow"), Joycraft has no mechanism to re-check it, and the repo's own check-shaped record (the folder map) decayed within weeks, so a human-corrected prose record with no re-deriver will drift faster while, per Ronacher, appearing more robust; joined to the team-lead's point that Helix runs the opposite direction (human-designed reference, reviewers enforce over code). I weighed this as nearly a flip. It does not flip because the refutation attacks the recording form and the missing reader, both of which are fixable and named by every skeptic, and not the practice's core: a memory of human corrections is load-bearing in Helix ("Helix records it in memory to improve every checkpoint that follows"), is a vendor-recommended pattern (record corrections; fresh-context verifiers), and the decision log already demonstrates in-repo that recorded rationale is reused. So the honest outcome is a narrowed claim, not a reversal.

**Key evidence:**
- Helix's architecture was human-designed, documented so reviewers have a standard to enforce, and enforced by two context-isolated reviewer agents checking code; the page does not say how feedback memory is stored or whether documentation is re-verified against code, and gives no cost or adoption numbers — https://shopify.engineering/helix (Talha Naqvi, 2026-09-21), fetched by the judge 2026-09-24: 'a highly opinionated architecture we designed for the new native apps'; 'thoroughly documented so reviewers have a standard to enforce'; 'Two independent, context-isolated reviewer agents check the new code against it'; 'Helix records it in memory to improve every checkpoint that follows'
- Joycraft's only two enforcement surfaces are permissions.deny and deny-patterns.txt, and semantic/judgment rules are ineligible and stay prose — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:13, 19-20, 33-40
- The verifier's oracle is the brief's Hard Constraints, its decisions: frontmatter, and the boundary file; the decision log and any architecture record are not inputs — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/skills/joycraft-verify.md Step 2.5 (lines 34-42) and the verifier prompt (lines 88-108)
- Setup-time onboarding deliberately does not read source to infer architecture because of token cost — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/skills/joycraft-gather-context.md:27
- The design skill already spawns codebase subagents, shows patterns as file:line snippets, records resolved decisions with rationale and rejected alternatives, and blocks on human review before handoff — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/skills/joycraft-design.md:40-45, 93-107, 270-278
- The decision log survived a six-panelist trial 6/6 with an in-repo demonstration of five prior rows reused; the Context Map is 'hopeful disclosure, not progressive disclosure'; must-read content is disqualified from the pointer tier — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/docs/research/2026-09-01-context-map-panel-verdict.md:16, 22, 24, 57
- The folder map is regenerated only on create-once generation paths and AGENTS.md lacks a docs/intent row although docs/intent exists; the repo's own check-shaped record has drifted — grep 2026-09-24: src/agents-md.ts:148, src/improve-claude-md.ts:414 (only callers of ensureFolderMapSection outside tests); diffFolderMap called only in tests/folder-map.test.ts:111-127; grep 'docs/intent' AGENTS.md returns nothing; ls docs/intent shows README.md and 2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft.md
- Context files, generated or developer-committed, do not generally improve task success and add over 20% inference cost, while instructions in them are followed — arXiv 2602.11988 (Gloaguen et al., ETH; v2 2026-06-23), as checked by three skeptics 2026-09-24
- The Theory Ledger (≤600 words, ≤7 deltas/session, independent verifier re-derives) was ranked #2 and never shipped; no theory.md, template, spec, or backlog item exists — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/docs/features/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-panel/research.md:41-43; grep across docs/backlog, docs/features, docs/specs 2026-09-24 hits only that research doc
- The escalation rule already routes any fact enforceable as architecture, a deny pattern, or a CI check to harden before prose — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/skills/joycraft-add-fact.md:24; /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/skills/joycraft-session-end.md:64
- Read telemetry stratifies mandated from voluntary reads per knowledge-layer doc, so a dead record is measurable — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/src/telemetry.ts:33-42, 65-86
- The only direct evidence for the practice is one colleague's self-report, and the pack itself records that it requires a CS background — /Users/compiler/Developer/joycraft/docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md:22 (§0)

**Skeptic disagreements:**
- Where the record lives. harness-expert: a project-scope mode of design/decide writing to the decision log, no new skill or doc. team-lead: fold into joycraft-design's per-feature review gate. ai-researcher: a distinct maturity gate on existing code only. evidence-auditor: primarily a verifier oracle, form secondary. Resolved in condition (1)-(3): decision-log rows + checks, as an opt-in mode of the design bookend.
- Whether architecture rules can become checks in Joycraft today. evidence-auditor: no, harden's two surfaces cannot express architecture rules (harden.md:35-37), so 'enforceable' is limited to what a verifier can check. harness-expert and ai-researcher: yes via CI dependency rules (dependency-cruiser), which are outside harden's surfaces. Both are correct on their own terms; condition (1a) admits project-owned CI checks, not only harden.
- Whether a short directive record could go in the always-loaded file. team-lead reads the ETH 'instructions are well followed' finding as support for an L1 placement of a short directive record. harness-expert, ai-researcher and evidence-auditor keep it out of L1 and out of the Context Map (context-map panel: L1 is directional content only). I side with the majority: L1 is not a home for architecture rules; that is the accretion Ronacher and the ThoughtWorks bloat paper describe.
- Pilot as a precondition. Only the ai-researcher requires a measured before/after delta before shipping; the other three accept the practice with structural conditions alone. I adopt the pilot (condition 5) because the sole positive evidence is an n=1 self-report and the maintainer's Q4 complaint is countable.
- Owner column on teams. team-lead requires one named owner and an owner column on rows; ai-researcher notes collaborative-setup records area owners but nothing ties a correction to an owner; harness-expert and evidence-auditor do not address ownership. Adopted as condition (4).
- Trigger for the maturity re-run. harness-expert: evidence triggers only (drift diff, NEVER_READ, verifier failure), never calendar. ai-researcher: 'a fixed cadence'. evidence-auditor: 'on a schedule'. I side with evidence triggers; a calendar re-run on a mature codebase is unpriced cost with no signal.
- Folder-map regeneration. harness-expert (and evidence pack §8.4) say ensureFolderMapSection 'is called only by tests'; ai-researcher correctly says it is reached from the generation paths (src/agents-md.ts:148, src/improve-claude-md.ts:414) and only diffFolderMap is tests-only. Same conclusion (never regenerated after creation), different fact.
- Cost of the setup instance. ai-researcher: greenfield has no code to defend, so setup reduces to design Sections 3-4. team-lead and harness-expert: the setup instance is a cost reversal of gather-context.md:27. evidence-auditor: practitioner-tier maturity gate at most. All reject a universal setup step; they differ on whether a greenfield instance is redundant or merely costly.
- Reading of the maintainer's Q2 'one path'. team-lead: Q2 and the CS-background constraint cannot both hold, so the maintainer must pick a fork (P11) or make it optional. harness-expert: fine for the maintainer-first path, breaks when corrector and implementer differ. I rule that an opt-in mode preserves one path better than a background fork.

**Citation problems:**
- Evidence pack §8.4 and the harness-expert state that ensureFolderMapSection 'is now called only by tests'. False: it is called from src/agents-md.ts:148 and src/improve-claude-md.ts:414 (the create-once generation paths). Only diffFolderMap is tests-only. The conclusion that the folder map is never regenerated after first creation survives; the literal claim does not.
- Evidence pack P10 and §0 apply Helix's 'This documentation makes adversarial review enforceable' to a human-corrected record produced by an agent-proposed architecture. The live page (fetched by the judge) says the architecture was designed by humans, the documentation is a standard for reviewers, and enforcement is two reviewer agents checking code. The quote holds; the transfer is not in the source.
- Evidence pack P10 says the Theory Ledger was 'called "the strongest single idea"'. The reading-fatigue brief (docs/research/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-brief.html:370) says 'arguably the strongest single idea'; the research.md:42 summary drops the hedge. Minor, flagged by the evidence-auditor.
- Evidence pack §4.1 SkillsBench figures are from a stale version per the ai-researcher's live fetch of v4 (2026-06-14): +16.6pp over 87 tasks, self-generated skills below baseline (-8.1 to -11.5pp) rather than 'no benefit', Software Engineering +11.6pp rather than +4.5pp, 13 of 87 tasks negative. Not P10-central; direction survives.
- The context-map panel verdict (2026-09-01, line 54) cites the ETH context-file study as arXiv 2601.20404 with a '+4% hand-written' figure; the evidence pack cites 2602.11988. No skeptic reconciled the two ids or checked the +4% figure.
- Ronacher's accretion quote (lucumr.pocoo.org 2026-06-23, evidence pack §1.8) was not re-fetched by any skeptic; relied on the pack's transcription.
- DCBench (arXiv 2605.08112) '+49% decision-compliance' as used by the context-map panel omits, per the ai-researcher's fetch, that the gain was confined to decisions invisible in source code and that the benchmark was authored by the vendor of the product under test; architecture decisions are mostly visible in code, so this figure supports P10 less than the lineage suggests.

**What would change the ruling:** Toward keep (claim stands with a plain human-read record): a with/without run on this repo or a colleague's project showing that a prose architecture record, read only by humans and not fed to verify, measurably reduces verify FINDINGS or the maintainer's hours of unshippable output; or telemetry showing the decision log is voluntarily read in more than 20% of feature-shaped sessions, which would weaken the 'no reader' objection. Toward flip (drop the practice): a pilot under conditions (1)-(2) in which the record is fed to verify and re-derived on drift and FINDINGS still do not fall; an ETH-style measurement on this repo showing the record adds cost with no delta; or an ACE-style collapse of the record's content after several maturity re-runs. Also load-bearing: any published account of how Helix stores feedback memory (prose vs checks vs examples) would settle whether the precedent supports a document at all.

**Human position moved?** Yes, on three points, with evidence. (1) Q4 'gates that cannot be overridden' and 'we have to close that gap' on unshippable output: the panel showed P10 as written is not a gate. verify.md Step 2.5 never reads an architecture record, harden.md:33-40 cannot convert one, and implement reads nothing under docs/context, so a setup-time document cannot close a gap on a path that never opens it. The Helix mechanism the maintainer admires is verifier-side (reviewers checking code against a human-designed standard), not a defense ceremony. The position moves from 'record the corrections' to 'the corrections become checks or verifier-oracle rows'. (2) Q1 'gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated': by the maintainer's own rule the architecture record is generated prose and therefore not part of the invariant; only the check or verifier input derived from it is. The §0 phrasing 'corrections become a core part of the context map' is the weakest possible form and is rejected by every skeptic on the context-map panel's 'hopeful disclosure' finding (verdict line 57). (3) Q2 'one path' versus the §0 constraint 'requires a CS background': the team-lead is right that both cannot hold for a mandatory setup step. The panel does not force a P11-style fork; it resolves it as an opt-in mode of the existing design bookend on existing code, which keeps one path. Not moved: the maintainer's belief that the practice itself reduces slop-on-slop. The skeptics could not refute it, only note it is one uncontrolled report confounded by the practitioner's skill, hence the pilot condition.

#### Skeptics

##### Agent-harness expert — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P10 as filed produces the one artifact class this repo has already ruled unenforceable: prose the model is hoped to read. Helix's "documentation makes adversarial review enforceable" holds on the live page, but the enforcement there is two context-isolated blocking reviewers plus "the reference *is* the spec" (code, not a document); the page says nothing about re-verifying recorded corrections as code changes (ABSENT). Joycraft has no mechanism to re-check an architecture record either: `harden` converts only command-regex/file-path rules and labels every semantic rule ineligible (src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:33-40, and :13 says "Prose is a rule the model merely hopes to follow"); the four shipped hook recipes are path guards and a non-blocking plan reminder (docs/templates/hooks/README.md:23-26); `verify`'s oracle is spec + brief + boundaries, never an architecture doc (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md, Step 2.5). Worse, the repo's own "check-shaped" architecture record already decayed: the folder map is create-once and `ensureFolderMapSection` is called only by tests (src/update-inventory.ts:225-262; evidence pack §8.4), and AGENTS.md has no `docs/intent` row although the folder exists (grep on AGENTS.md returns nothing). A generated, machine-derivable map drifted in three weeks; a human-corrected prose record with no re-deriver will drift faster and, per Ronacher, "each iteration adds another small defense… less understandable while appearing more robust" (evidence §1.8). Finally it duplicates `design`, which already spawns codebase subagents, cites `file:line` snippets, records Resolved Design Decisions and option-bearing Open Questions (src/skills/joycraft-design.md:40-107), and it reverses `gather-context`'s explicit setup-time decision not to run a code-inference scan for cost (src/skills/joycraft-gather-context.md:27).

**Qualification:** P10 survives only under all of: (1) every human correction terminates in one of exactly two forms in the same commit — a machine check (dependency-cruiser/ArchUnit-style dependency rule, lint rule, protected-path hook, or test) or an entry in a capped ledger (≤600 words, the reading-fatigue Theory Ledger's shape) that a fresh-context verifier re-derives at the PR bookend; a correction that fits neither is discarded, not recorded; (2) it runs as a project-scope mode of `design`/`decide` writing to the decision log (the one context doc all six panelists kept), not a new skill or a new doc; (3) on a mature codebase the agent extracts rules from existing code and the human confirms (Helix's "reference is the spec"), rather than proposing-and-defending from scratch; (4) the maturity re-run is triggered by evidence (drift diff, telemetry NEVER_READ, verifier failure), not by calendar. Without (1) it is advice, and the maintainer's own Q4 asks for gates that cannot be overridden.

**On the human's position:** The maintainer filed no P10-specific checkpoint answer; the position comes from §0 (colleague's practice, "much less slop, especially the 'slop on slop' that accretes as a project matures"; "requires a CS background") and bears on Q1 and Q4. Q1: "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed; process prose generated." P10 as written generates prose and then treats it as a gate — that is the exact category confusion Q1 rules out. Q4: "Gates that cannot be overridden… in recent sessions I've been getting some slop that took hours and that was not shippable, we have to close that gap." An architecture record nobody re-checks cannot close a shippability gap; it can only describe what should have happened. The maintainer's own harness says so: harden.md:13 ("Prose is a rule the model merely hopes to follow") and session-end.md:64 routes any fact "enforceable as architecture, a deny pattern, or a CI check" to harden, not prose. So my lens moves the position in one direction: keep the session, but change what a correction is allowed to become — a check in the same commit, or a capped ledger entry that a fresh-context verifier re-derives; otherwise discard it. On "requires a CS background": for the maintainer-first path (Q2) this is fine, but the moment corrector and implementer differ across the fifteen colleagues, only the check form binds the implementer; the prose form binds nobody who did not attend the session. The "defend with code examples" ritual is the cheap, visible part and the least valuable: on a mature codebase the code already is the defense (Helix: "the reference is the spec"); let the agent extract rules from it and have the human confirm.

##### Team lead, five engineers — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** "Enforceable architecture record" is a category error in Joycraft as wired. The only enforcement surfaces are deny-patterns.txt and permissions.deny (src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:19-20), and harden explicitly classes semantic/judgment rules as ineligible and leaves them as prose (harden.md:33-40). An architecture correction ("no, repositories go through the service layer") is exactly that class. The one independent verifier Joycraft has reads spec + brief hard constraints + decisions frontmatter + boundaries (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md:34-42); it never reads an architecture record or the decision log. So after the human corrects, nothing re-checks the correction as code drifts — the proposition's own skeptic angle is confirmed by the repo. On a five-person team that is fatal: five engineers each get a different agent-proposed architecture, correct it differently (juniors cannot correct at all — the pack's own constraint, evidence §0 line 23: "requires a CS background"), the record has no owner column (src/templates/context/decision-log.md: Date | Decision | Why | Alternatives | Revisit When), and the reviewer now carries two review loads — the diff and whether the diff honored an un-machine-checked document. Helix, the cited precedent, runs the opposite direction: a human-designed, fixed reference architecture that agents implement, enforced by two context-isolated reviewer agents, not by the document (shopify.engineering/helix, checked 2026-09-24). And Joycraft already has this step per feature: design spawns subagents to read code (joycraft-design.md:42), shows patterns as code snippets with file:line (93-95), states resolved decisions with rationale (99-104), the human corrects at a blocking review gate (277, 303-304), and decide stamps the result into the decision log (joycraft-decide.md:253). A setup-time repeat that reads the whole codebase reverses gather-context's deliberate cost decision (joycraft-gather-context.md:27: "Do NOT auto-run a code-inference scan") with no new evidence.

**Qualification:** P10 stands for a team only under all four conditions: (1) every correction terminates as a machine check (harden deny pattern, CI assertion, or lint) or as a decision-log row with an explicit owner and 'Revisit when' — never as free prose in the context map or AGENTS.md; (2) that record becomes an oracle input to joycraft-verify Step 2.5 so a fresh-context verifier re-derives it against the code at every PR bookend (the Theory Ledger's 'independent verifier re-derives periodically'), and drift fails the gate instead of waiting for a human to notice; (3) on a team, exactly one named owner runs the defense session and commits the record; the other engineers' sessions read it as a constraint and may only file corrections through the same owner-stamped path, never re-propose the architecture; (4) it is a per-feature step at the design bookend for practitioners (folded into joycraft-design, which already does 80% of it), not a mandatory setup step on the 'one path' — gated on P11's background flag or on the owner opting in. Without (1) and (2) it is refuted: a document the human alone verifies is exactly the 'hopeful disclosure' the last panel condemned. Without (3) it produces five divergent architecture records for one codebase.

##### AI researcher — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P10 rests on zero measured deltas and on an analogy that does not transfer. The only direct evidence is one colleague's self-report ("He reports much less slop", evidence pack §0, docs/research/2026-09-24-dynamic-joycraft-evidence.md:22), n=1, no baseline, not on Joycraft. The Helix quote holds verbatim (shopify.engineering/helix, 2026-09-21), but in Helix the documentation is an upfront engineer-written reference for a fixed target architecture, and enforcement comes from two context-isolated reviewer agents plus blocking gates, not from the document; the article says nothing about how memory is stored or how docs stay in sync with code (confirmed absent on live fetch). The closest measured analog to "an architecture record in the repo's context files" is the ETH study (arXiv 2602.11988, 2026-02-12, rev 2026-06-23): repository context files, developer-written or LLM-generated, "do not generally improve task success rates, while increasing inference cost by over 20% on average". The one positive result, DCBench (arXiv 2605.08112, 2026-04-27, +49pp decision compliance, 46%→95%), explicitly found the baseline already at full compliance on decisions visible in the source code; the gain lived entirely on decisions invisible in code (product/persona/customer context). Architecture decisions are mostly visible in code, so DCBench's gain lands where P10 contributes least. In-repo, the record has no reader on the path where the maintainer says the slop occurs: joycraft-verify's oracle is brief Hard Constraints + brief decisions frontmatter + boundary file (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md:34-42, 100) and never docs/context/decision-log.md; joycraft-implement reads no docs/context file at all (grep empty); design reads the decision log via a grep capped at 5 rows (src/skills/joycraft-design.md:17-30). The repo already demonstrates the drift failure P10 would repeat: tune.md:63 says upgrade regenerates the folder map, but ensureFolderMapSection is reached only from the generation paths (src/agents-md.ts:148, src/improve-claude-md.ts:414) and diffFolderMap only from tests/folder-map.test.ts:111-127, while AGENTS.md is create-once (src/update-inventory.ts:236-262) — so the one check-shaped architecture artifact Joycraft ships is never re-checked. A prose architecture record would be worse: no check at all.

**Qualification:** P10 stands only under all three conditions: (1) every correction from the session terminates as a machine check (dependency rule, deny pattern, CI assertion, via harden) or as a decision-log row, never as a standalone prose architecture record; (2) joycraft-verify's oracle (verify.md:34-42) is extended to read those rows, and a fresh-context re-derivation of the record against code runs at a fixed cadence, so a reader exists on the implement path; (3) it ships as a maturity gate on existing code, not a greenfield setup step, and only after a pilot measures a delta (verify FINDINGS rate, or a DCBench-style compliance probe on the project's own corrections) against sessions without it. Absent (1)-(2) the record is hopeful disclosure that the ETH null result says costs >20% for nothing; absent (3) the sole evidence remains one uncontrolled self-report.

##### Evidence auditor — qualified

**Strongest refutation:** P10's word "enforceable" has no citation behind it and no mechanism in the repo. Helix (shopify.engineering/helix, fetched 2026-09-24) says "This documentation makes adversarial review enforceable" — but the documentation there is an architecture the engineers wrote up front, and enforcement is "Two independent, context-isolated reviewer agents check the new code against it." The page does not say that engineer corrections become a document, nor how "memory" is stored (the pack's own "Not stated" caveat, §0 line 20, is correct). So Helix supports "reviewers check code against a written architecture," not "human corrections accrete into a record." The second pillar, the Theory Ledger, is a proposal citing a proposal: no docs/context/theory.md or template exists, and the brief hedges it as "arguably the strongest single idea" (docs/research/2026-07-20-reading-fatigue-brief.html:370) — the pack drops "arguably". The third pillar is one colleague's unquantified anecdote (§0 line 22). Meanwhile the one controlled study in the pack cuts against a read-on-demand record: Gloaguen et al. v2 (arXiv 2602.11988, 2026-06-23) finds context files, "both LLM-generated and developer-committed," "do not generally improve task success rates, while increasing inference cost by over 20% on average," and "repository overviews ... are not helpful." In the repo today nothing re-checks the corrections as code drifts: verify's oracle is the brief's Hard Constraints, its decisions: frontmatter, and AGENTS.md boundaries (src/skills/joycraft-verify.md:38-42) — not decision-log.md or dangerous-assumptions.md; harden can only enforce rules statable "as a command regex or file-path pattern" (src/skills/joycraft-harden.md:35-37) and names permissions.deny plus deny-patterns.txt as "the only two enforcement surfaces" (harden.md:20); no skill acts on the decision log's "Revisit When" column (only decide.md:255 writes it). An architecture record written today would be hopeful disclosure by the context-map panel's own definition (2026-09-01 verdict line 57): the Context Map has one row (AGENTS.md:189-191).

**Qualification:** P10 stands only under all of: (1) the record is consumed as an oracle by an independent verifier (verify Step 2.5 and any Helix-style reviewer gate) and re-derived from code by a fresh-context subagent on a schedule, with diffs surfaced — not merely written to docs/context and pointed at from the Context Map; (2) it is a maturity gate for the practitioner path, not a universal setup step, because gather-context.md:27 forbids the code scan by default and the pack itself says the practice needs a CS background; (3) 'enforceable' is limited to what a verifier can check — architecture rules cannot become deny patterns (harden.md:35-37); (4) the Theory Ledger and the colleague's report are labeled as untested proposals, not evidence, until a with/without run exists.

**Evidence against the refutation:**

- Anthropic's live guidance endorses the verifier half of the Theory Ledger and a corrections memory. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5, fetched 2026-09-24: "Separate, fresh-context verifier subagents tend to outperform self-critique"; "Record corrections and confirmed approaches alike, including why they mattered."

**Citations checked:**

The pack's 'Not stated' list (memory storage, scope, numbers) is accurate. But the quote supports reviewers-check-against-docs, not corrections-become-docs.
- arXiv 2602.11988 Gloaguen et al., ETH — context files do not generally improve task success, >20% cost (§4.7): **holds** — Abstract wording and 20% figure exact; v2 dated 2026-06-23 (pack cites v1 date 2026-02-12, still correct). Adds 'repository overviews ... are not helpful', which the pack omits.

'Depends critically on feedback quality' is a paraphrase of 'effectiveness depends on the availability of signals that allow the Reflector and Curator to make sound judgments.'
- Prompting Claude Fable 5 — fresh-context verifiers beat self-critique; skills for prior models too prescriptive; fabricated status reports nearly eliminated (§4.6): **holds** — All three quotes verbatim on the live page.

But the brief says 'arguably the strongest single idea' (brief.html:370); the pack drops the hedge and presents a judges' aside as a verdict.

**Unverified:**
- The colleague's (Atharva Vaidya) practice and its 'much less slop' outcome — anecdote, n=1, no artifact, no numbers; treated as motivation, not evidence.
- Whether Helix's 'memory' is a human-readable architecture document that reviewer agents read — the page does not say.
- The reading-fatigue brief's claim that the decision log 'grew 14× past its template' (brief.html:346,374) — not re-derived; decision-log.md is 111 lines today.

**On the human's position:** Section 10 has no direct answer on P10; the nearest are Q4 and the §0 anecdote. Q4: "we are already doing alot of what helix is doing, but I think what they do better is that once they actually get tot he implementation loop it's basically sit back and relax and have full confidence... we have to close that gap." Taken at its word, the maintainer's own diagnosis argues against P10 as framed: the Helix mechanism that produces that confidence is two isolated reviewers checking code against a written architecture plus blocking gates — a verifier-side change — not a setup-time defense session whose output is a document. Joycraft already has the reviewer half's skeleton (verify.md:34-42 feeds stamped decisions to a fresh subagent); what it lacks is the architecture doc as an oracle input and a re-derivation pass. The §0 framing ("corrections become a core part of the context map") is the weakest version: the context map is hopeful disclosure with one row, and Gloaguen's controlled result says read-on-demand context files do not lift task success. My lens moves the position this far: P10 survives only if 'enforceable architecture record' is operationalized as a verifier oracle (an input to verify and to Helix-style reviewers, with a periodic independent re-derivation diffed against code, as the Theory Ledger proposed), never as a context-map pointer. As a setup step it also collides with gather-context.md:27's explicit no-code-scan cost rule and with the constraint the maintainer himself recorded — 'requires a CS background, so it is useless for Joycraft's novice users' — so it is a practitioner-tier maturity gate at most, and the Q2 'one path' answer needs a fork to accommodate it.


### P11 — A user technical-background profile forks the abstraction level

**Ruling: FLIP.** P11 does not stand. A setup-time technical-background profile that forks which gates run, how much ceremony applies, and what artifacts show contradicts the maintainer's own Q1 invariant (gates + lifecycle + artifacts fixed) and Q2 (one path), has no per-user home in Joycraft's file model without breaking committed team artifacts, rests on a single unmeasured anecdote from a non-user, and its only shipped precedent (BMAD `user_skill_level`) was removed on 2026-08-09. Replace with: altitude is a per-project property set once by the repo owner next to the Execution Profile in AGENTS.md; the only per-user residue is an uncommitted explanation-depth preference that changes presentation, never gates, ceremony, or committed content.

**Claim as argued:** Setup captures the user's technical background and forks vocabulary, which gates run, how much ceremony, and what artifacts show, so novices and practitioners walk one path at different altitudes. Skeptic angles: self-assessed skill is unreliable and drifts (infer from behavior instead?); does the fork change content or only vocabulary; is the novice path Joycraft's market at all; a per-user fork conflicts with committed shared artifacts on a team; the execution profile in AGENTS.md is per-harness, not per-user.

**Replacement claim:** Altitude belongs to the project, not the person. Whoever owns the repo sets it once, in AGENTS.md beside the Execution Profile, identical for every author; gates, ceremony, checkpoint questions, specs, decision rows, and PR bodies are one path per project. The P10 architecture-defense gate runs for everyone; the agent carries the CS load by explaining each decision in STE, it does not skip the gate for anyone. The one per-user knob is an uncommitted, revocable explanation-depth preference living in docs/.joycraft/local/ (or the host's per-user output style on Claude Code), inside the STE contract (plainer sentences, not a second vocabulary), that changes how results are explained and nothing else. Build even that only after one named daily user who cannot read a diff exists, and instrument the brief's existing unread `User expertise` field first to see whether it ever changes an outcome.

**Condition:** The residue (per-user explanation depth) holds only if all four are true: (1) it is stored uncommitted (docs/.joycraft/local/ or .claude/settings.local.json), (2) it changes no gate, no ceremony count, and no committed artifact, (3) it stays inside the STE output contract rather than forking vocabulary, and (4) a named user who needs it is using Joycraft daily. If the profile gates any gate or writes to any committed file, the proposition is refuted for any project with more than one author.

**Judge's reasoning:** Four independent grounds, each sufficient. (1) Frame contradiction: the maintainer fixed "Gates + lifecycle + artifacts" as the invariant (§10 Q1) and confirmed "one path" (§10 Q2) with the prediction that skill spread "becomes a non issue" as the harness drives more. P11's fork of "which gates run, how much ceremony, what the artifacts show" varies exactly what Q1 fixes; strip that and only vocabulary remains, which frontier models adapt per reader without a stored profile and which the STE contract (src/templates/reference/output-style.md, rule 10: one word for one concept) already fixes for everyone. (2) No home: the Execution Profile is "team-shared data the human owns and hand-edits", per-harness, ONE_HOME (src/execution-profile.ts:9-11); AGENTS.md is create-once and never regenerated (src/update-inventory.ts:228-261); the manifest has only vendor|create-once|config-patch kinds (src/install-manifest.ts:30); the sole gitignored per-user home is docs/.joycraft/local/ (.gitignore:15), which today holds one presentation flag (autoOpen, joycraft-tune.md:89). A profile that changes committed artifacts therefore either lives in a shared file (every author gets the same altitude, so it is a project setting) or needs new machinery for an unproven need. (3) No demand signal: the brief template has carried `User expertise: [comfortable / learning / needs guidance]` (src/skills/joycraft-new-feature.md:181) and nothing in src/skills, src/*.ts, src/templates, or tests consumes it (verified grep: only the template line and its generated bundle copies). The pack's positive case is one secondhand practice from a colleague who does not use Joycraft (§0), and no named Joycraft user cannot read a diff. (4) Precedent and measurement point the other way: BMAD removed `user_skill_level` tailoring in v6.11.0 (verified live, CHANGELOG line under "## v6.11.0 - 2026-08-09"); the Bing Copilot study (arXiv 2502.18685) found expert-register responses correlate with positive UX regardless of user level while under-pitching hurts; arXiv 2608.10319 found pooled generic skills beat per-developer personalized ones; every "adapt to capability" result in the pack (§4.4, §4.5) is about backbone model tier with no human variable. The self-assessment-reliability angle is weaker than the pack implies (Feigenspan ρ=0.539 for a single programming-experience question; McIntosh r=0.43-0.47 in general) and I do not rest the ruling on it; the drift problem is real though, since the product's stated job is to move the user up levels and no mechanism re-scores a setup snapshot. The team-lead's "qualified" and the three "refuted" verdicts converge on the same residue, and that residue is not "forks the abstraction level"; it is a verbosity preference. Hence flip, with the replacement claim naming where altitude actually lives.

**Strongest refutation considered:** The strongest case FOR P11: the maintainer explicitly asked for a novice-vibe-coder lens (Q7) and describes his fifteen colleagues as "mixed skill"; the P10 architecture-defense practice is reported to need a CS background, so some user-keyed gating of P10 answers a real need; a per-user, per-project gitignored home already exists (docs/.joycraft/local/, and Claude Code's settings.local.json is documented as "personal exceptions don't need a commit"); programmer self-estimate correlates ρ=0.539 with measured comprehension, so the input is not useless; and expertise alignment does matter in one direction (arXiv 2502.18685: pitching below an expert hurts). I weighed this and it does not rescue P11 as written: it supports a per-user presentation preference, not a fork of gates or artifacts, and the P10 need is better met by explaining the defense at the reader's level than by skipping it, since skipping it makes the gate advisory by author, which Q4 ("gates that cannot be overridden") rejects. The self-estimate correlation is also about static programming experience, not the AI-assisted level that the product intends to change.
